Course Descriptions

courses.label: ACC 101
courses.title: Introductory Accounting |
paras: An introduction to the principles and practices underlying the historical-cost income determination model. Restricted to students required by their program to take ACC 101, or to students registered in ECON 101, ACC 131, and CS 112 or 140.

courses.label: ACC 102
courses.title: Introductory Accounting II
paras: Acontinuation of Accounting 101. Restricted to students who have obtained at least a “C-” in ACC 1017.

courses.label: ACC 121
courses.title: Understanding and Using Financial Accounting Information
paras: This course is designed for nonaccounting majors to help them_ understand and analyze financial statements.

courses.label: ACC 122
courses.title: Understanding and Using Managerial Accounting Information
paras: This course is designed for nonaccounting majors. The use of accounting information to assist in planning, control and managerial decision-making will be examined.

courses.label: ACC 131
courses.title: Management I/II
paras: The functional areas of business: finance, personnel administration, production, marketing and accounting are examined within differing organizational structures. Coverage
also includes study of the principles of etfective management and the financial system in Canada as a source of corporate capital.
Prereq: ACC 131 is a prerequisite for ACC 132.

courses.label: ACC 231
courses.title: Business Law
paras: . Particular attention is given to the law relating to contracts and business organizations. Other areas of study include sources of law, the judicial process, real and personal property, torts, agency, credit, and negotiable instruments.

courses.label: ACC 251
courses.title: Auditing !
paras: An examination of the standards developed by the accounting profession which guide professional accountants in performing the attest function. Elements of effective control structures and the concept of audit evidence are examined.
Prereq: ACC 291

courses.label: ACC 281
courses.title: Introductory Managerial Accounting
paras: An introduction to the principles and practices of managerial accounting. Prereq: ACC 102

courses.label: ACC 291
courses.title: Financial Accounting |
paras: A first course in intermediate financial accounting dealing with the theory and practice of financial statement preparation and reporting. The emphasis will be on asset valuation and the related impact on income measurement.
Prereq: ACC 281

courses.label: ACC 292
courses.title: Financial Accounting I
paras: This course completes the coverage of intermediate financial accounting. It deals with problems related to the measurement of liabilities, accounting for income taxes and the reporting and measuring of corporate equities. Prereq: ACC 291

courses.label: ACC 371
courses.title: Managerial Finance |
paras: Analytic techniques for financial decision-making will be considered within a conceptual framework. Emphasis is placed upon the long-term investment, capital structure and distribution decisions. Developments in capital asset pricing, and efficient markets will be examined.
Prereq: ECON 101 or 102; 221 and
AGC 291

courses.label: ACC 372
courses.title: Managerial Finance II
paras: The theoretical concepts examined in Accounting 371 will be applied within the context of the Canadian economy. Topics examined will include interest rate determination, capital markets, and risk/return characteristics of financing alternatives. .
Prereq: ACC 371

courses.label: ACC 381
courses.title: Managerial Accounting |
paras: The development and use of accounting information in performing the managerial functions of planning, controlling, decision making and performance evaluation. Emphasis is on analysis of costs rather than procedural aspects of costing systems.
Prereq: ACC 291 and a course in Statistics.

courses.label: ACC 382
courses.title: Managerial Accounting II
paras: Consideration of more complex topics in management planning and control. Emphasis is on cost accumulation systems, transfer pricing and applications of quantitative methods to management accounting.
Prereq: ACC 381

courses.label: ACC 401
courses.title: Accounting Theory
paras: A review of accounting theory asa background for applying underlying concepts to current accounting problems. Emphasis is on current literature, with a major term paper required.
Prereq: ACC 371 and 491

courses.label: ACC 402
courses.title: Research
paras: An introduction to research methodology and current research in accounting.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 401 .

Accounting

courses.label: ACC 411
courses.title: Statistical Methods for Accountants
paras: An introduction to the statistical tools most useful to the accountant; linear and non-linear regression, sampling and time-series analysis. Available software analysis packages wil! be paid.
Prereq: Registration in Year 3 of any Faculty of Arts Accounting program.

courses.label: ACC 412
courses.title: Computer Applications in Business
paras: An introduction to the operation of mainframe and microcomputer systems. Emphasis will be placed on software packages that have particular application to accounting transaction processing and financial planning. Prereq: Registration in Year 3 of any Faculty of Arts Accounting program

courses.label: ACC 414
courses.title: Special Topics
paras: Admission by consent of instructor.

courses.label: ACC 431
courses.title: Management Decisions
paras: A case course; examines the accountant’s participation in decisions drawn from functional areas (marketing, production) in policy and strategy formulation situations, and in evaluation of the impact of government regulation and policy.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3.

courses.label: ACC 441
courses.title: Accounting Information Systems
paras: Investigates the concepts and principles of management information systems. Concentration is on the role of accounting information in the planning/ decision-making process and the design and implementation of accounting information systems. Prereq: ACC 382.

courses.label: ACC 451
courses.title: Auditing il
paras: An examination of the elements involved in the determination of the extent of audit testing. Quantitative models will be employed in developing and evaluating examination samples. Prereq: Registration in AP 3.

courses.label: ACC 452
paras: Auditing III
An examination of current topics affecting public accounting practice. Topics will also include legal, ethical and statutory guidelines.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 451.

courses.label: ACC 453
courses.title: Computer Audit and Control
paras: The evaluation of controls ina computerized environment, the impact’ of the computer on the audit approach and the utilization of the computer in conducting audit testing are
. considered.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 441.

courses.label: ACC 454
courses.title: Operationa! Auditing
paras: An extension of the basic audit to include the appraisal and establishment of administrative and operational controls; and the evaluation of the efficiency of individual business functions.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3.

courses.label: ACC 461
courses.title: Taxation |
paras: A course in the interpretation in application of the major provisions of the Income Tax Act through an analysis of court decisions, Revenue Canada's publications, and practical problem situations.
Prereq: Completion of or registration in ACC 102.

courses.label: ACC 462
courses.title: Taxation Il
paras: A continuation of ACC 461. Prereq: ACC 461.

courses.label: ACC 463
courses.title: Taxation IH
paras: A course which integrates the topics covered in ACC 461 and 462 for individual and corporate tax planning through a study of trusts, partnerships, corporate reorganizations and estate planning.
Prereq: ACC 462 and registration in Honours Accounting.

courses.label: ACC 464
courses.title: Taxation: Business and Property Income
paras: An in-depth study of the computation of business and property income with an emphasis on the case law that has developed in this area.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and
ACC 463.

courses.label: ACC 465
courses.title: Taxation: Corporate Reorganizations
paras: An in-depth study of the provisions of the income Tax Act relating to corporate reorganizations including share exchanges, amalgamations, and winding up a corporation.
Prereq: Registration AP 3 and ACC 463.

courses.label: ACC 466
courses.title: Taxation: Partnerships and Trusts
paras: An examination of tax legislation pertaining to the taxation of partnerships and their members, and trusts and their beneficiaries.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 463

courses.label: ACC 467
courses.title: International Taxation
paras: An examination of topics including shareholders of non-resident corporations and tax on Canadian income of non-residents. The course will also examine the effects on Canadian residents of the United States’ tax legislation.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 463.

courses.label: ACC 468
courses.title: Taxation: Estate Planning
paras: A comprehensive review of Canadian income tax legislation with a focus on techniques and consequences of estate planning.
Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 463.

courses.label: ACC 469
courses.title: Taxation: Purchase and Sale of a Business
paras: A comprehensive review of Canadian income tax legislation and related areas with a focus on a comparison of alternative methads and their consequences on purchase and sale of a business. Prereq: Registration in AP 3 and ACC 463.

courses.label: ACC 471
courses.title: Investments
paras: The objective of this course is to introduce the student to concepts of investment selection, purchase and management. The student should obtain a knowledge of security markets and the risk/return characteristics of forms of investment.
Prereq: ACC 371

courses.label: ACC 481
courses.title: Controllership
paras: A comprehensive insight into the problems facing top management accounting executives. Course includes a number of cases designed to expose students to real world situations requiring qualitative and quantitative analysis.
Prereq: ACC 382

paras: Accounting

courses.label: ACC 491

introductory Notes

ANTH 101 courses introduce physical anthropology and archaeology. ANTH 102 courses introduce social-cultural anthropology. The letter designations (A,B) indicate the special approach of the course. A student may take introductory courses in any order. ANTH 101, ANTH 102A or 1028, or ANTH 103 may be taken first and any combination may be taken together.

courses.label: ANTH 101
courses.title: Human and Cultural Evolution
paras: An overview of Physica! Anthropology and Archaeology. Lectures on living and fossil primates, the fossil evidence for the origins and development of man, modern races, and archaeological evidence for the origins and development of culture.
Required for Anthropology Honours students and Majors.

courses.label: ANTH 102A
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Cultural Anthropology
paras: The dynamic nature of socio-cultural systems is examined. Topics include language, technology, social organization, economics, politics, and religion. Data are drawn from a broad ethnographic base, including both “primitive” cultures and modern, developed societies.
A student may not take both ANTH 102A and ANTH 102B for credit. Anthropology Honours students and Majors must take ANTH 102A or ANTH 102B.

courses.label: ANTH 102B
courses.title: Anthropology Through Science Fiction
paras: Basic anthropological concepts, such as biological and cultural evolution, culture, human adaptability, and culture contact will be explored through examples from science fiction and related anthropological studies.
A Student may not take both ANTH 102A and ANTH 102B for credit. Anthropology Honours students and Majors must take ANTH 102A or ANTH 1028.

courses.label: ANTH 103
courses.title: The Nature of Language
paras: A general introduction to the scientific study of language. Lectures on the nature of human language as compared with animal communication, some of the basic methods of historical and descriptive linguistics, and the importance of language in culture and society.
Honours students and Majors in Anthropology are required to take ANTH 103, ANTH 283, or ANTH 290.

courses.label: ANTH 201
courses.title: Principles of Archaeology
paras: An introduction to the working assumptions, analytic approaches, and integrative and descriptive methods of archaeological anthropology.
Required for Anthropology Honours students and Majors.

Anthropology

courses.label: ANTH 202
courses.title: Principles of Sociai Organization
paras: An introduction to basic concepts used by social anthropologists for the analysis of social, economic, potitical and ideational systems.
Prereq: ANTH 102A or ANTH 102B or permission of instructor. Required for Anthropology Honours students and Majors.

courses.label: ANTH 203
courses.title: Prehistoric Man in North America
paras: This is a general introduction to North American Archaeology. The traditional cultural ecological approach is compared and contrasted with the more revolutionary ideas recently expounded by popular writers.

courses.label: ANTH 221
courses.title: « Prehistoric Archaeology: Olid World II
paras: Examination of the transition to an economy based on food production, the spread of food producing economies, the rise of civilization. Areas and periods of emphasis will vary from year to year.
Not acceptable for Honours Anthropology credit.

courses.label: ANTH 228
courses.title: Peoples of the Pacific
paras: A comparative ethnologica! survey of selected indigenous societies in the Pacific Region.

courses.label: ANTH 230
courses.title: Indians of Canada
paras: The cultures of Canadian Indians are described as they existed when initially contacted by Europeans. Consideration is given to economic adaptation, social organization, political structure, material culture, ritual, and mythology. Prereq: Second year standing.
By correspondence only for 1983-84.

courses.label: ANTH 233
courses.title: Eskimo Cultures
paras: Eskimo cultures of Alaska, Canada, and Greenland from the time of European and Asian contact to the present. Administrative systems imposed on the Eskimo will be analyzed and compared, as will the contemporary problems these communities face today.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: ANTH 241
courses.title: The Contemporary Canadian indian Scene
paras: An analysis of present-day Canadian Indian politics, economics, social organization, and education. The emergence of pan-Indianism and farge-scale Indian organizations will be examined as responses to the Federal Government's policy of withdrawing and decentralizing administrative services for native people.

courses.label: ANTH 258
courses.title: Anthropology and the Future of Man
paras: Anthropological theories pertaining to culture’ change and cultural evolution are examined in the context of the modern world. Long and short term trends in technology are examined using data from Archaeology, Ethnography, History, Technology and Science.
Prereq: ANTH 101 or 102 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 260
courses.title: Human Evolution
paras: Data, methods, and theory in the study of the origin and evolution of humans are surveyed. Topics will inctude osteology, growth and development, the fossil record, and genetics.
Prereq: ANTH 101 or permission of the instructor.
Required for Anthropology Honours students and Majors. By correspondence only for 1983 ;84.

courses.label: ANTH 261
courses.title: Primate Behaviour
paras: An introduction to the behaviour of non-human primates and its relevance to human development. Topics will inctude social organization, rote of : behaviour, and communication
patterns, as well as the history of primate studies.

courses.label: ANTH 290
courses.title: Language and Cuiture
paras: An examination of language as it reflects the culture of the speakers. Focus will be on exploring aspects of vocabulary and special usages for their cultural relevance, with illustrations from a variety of languages.
Prereq: One half-course from each of linguistics and socio-cultural anthropology.
Honours students and Majors in Anthropology are required to take ANTH 103, ANTH 283, or ANTH 290.

courses.label: ANTH 300
courses.title: Design of Anthropological Inquiry
paras: This course systematically examines research design and methodology in anthropology.
Prereq: ANTH 101, ANTH 102A or ANTH 102B.
Required for all Anthropology Honours Students.

courses.label: ANTH 311
courses.title: Magic, Witchcraft and Religion
paras: An introduction to the way in which anthropologists study the system of ° behaviour and belief known as religion.

courses.label: ANTH 321
courses.title: Recent Prehistory in the Old World
paras: Cultural development from the agri- ©
cultural revolution to the rise of literacy.
Special attention to the development of agriculture as a means of subsistence and to the rise of early civilization. Areas and periods of emphasis will vary from year to year.
Prereq: ANTH 201 or permission of the instructor.
Primarily for Honours Anthropology Students.

courses.label: ANTH 330
courses.title: Cultural Ecology
paras: An examination of the relationships among environment, technology, society, and culture. The increasing levels of complexity will be considered in the context of hunting and foraging bands, horticultural tribes and chiefdoms, pastoral tribes and agricultural peasantry.
Prereq: Full credit in Anthropology or consent of the instructor.
Required for alf Anthropology Honours students and Majors.

courses.label: ANTH 345
courses.title: Special Problems in Anthropology
paras: Directed independent research. Prereq: Permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 347
courses.title: Special Problems Topic
paras: Directed independent research. Prereq: Permission of instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 350
courses.title: Sex Roles in Anthropology
paras: A seminar to investigate the role of the sexes in human evolution and the ways in which gender categories and the concept of sex roles are considered in anthropological literature.

courses.title: Comparative Policies on Native Minorities
paras: A comparative survey of government policies on native minorities with emphasis on recent attempts to involve native groups in the policy-making processes. The course will compare policy approaches to Canadian Indians and Metis, Australian Aboriginals, New Zealand Maoris and Scandinavian Samis (Lapps). : Prereg: One of ANTH 102A or 1028, or P SCI 101 or 102M, or SOC 101. .

courses.label: ANTH 370
courses.title: Ethnographic Field Methods
paras: The techniques and problems of ethnographic field work will be explored. Emphasis wilt be on field work in contemporary society. Students will be expected to complete a field project of their own.
Prereq: ANTH 202 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: ANTH 373
courses.title: Archaeological Reporting
paras: Various ways of processing archaeological data will be demonstrated and discussed. The major emphasis will be on writing up archaeological reports. Primarily for Honours Anthropology students.
Prereq: Permission of the instructor.

paras: Guided reading in a selected portion of the anthropological literature.

courses.title: Social and Cultural Change
paras: An analysis of contemporary thought on culture contact and cultural evolution. The concepts to be explored might include integration, assimilation, conflict, nativistic reactions, and general and specific evolution.
Prereq: One credit in socio-cultural anthropology.

courses.label: ARCH 283
courses.title: Preservation Practice-Technology and Technique
paras: An introduction to the field of preservation of older buildings, particularly in Canada; dealing mainly with older building technology, typical probiems in the preservation field and indicated steps toward solution.

courses.label: ARCH 142
courses.title: Iconography 1
paras: Conventions

Selected schemes of order, such as fate, Providence, natural law, the human will, as expressed in plays, poems, and fiction from various ages; selected conventions in literature, cinema, and the visual arts; the development of one or two archetypal symbols in literature and the visual arts; directed to lead into more detailed studies of symbolic patterns in Iconography 2.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 143
courses.title: Iconography 2
paras: A survey of the symbolic Nature of the Environment

A study centred on ancient life to initiate the student into the stream of cultural history and the complex problems of what the artist is, the quality of human existence, culture, environment, as well as the working of the icon from raw state of perceived image to its function as an expressive symbol in poetry, music, dance, architecture and other works of art; a study of modern work in comparison to an ancient achievement.
Prereq: ARCH 142

courses.label: ARCH 244
courses.title: History of Gardens of Europe and Western Asia
paras: The study of gardens as works of art reconciling man with his wortd. Gardens of Europe and Western Asia are studied as responses to specific human needs, the stress and aspirations of an age, and to the climate and landscape of the tand in which they were created.

courses.title: Survey of Contemporary Architecture Formative years in Europe, early North
paras: American scene. Analyses of important buildings of twentieth century. Philosophies of internationally known architects and designers. Study of the development of architectural styles, trends and schools of thought in North America and other countries.
Prereq: Second year standing

courses.label: ARCH 246
courses.title: Foundations of Europe
paras: Sense of Periods and Styles Recognition of patterns of life and concepts of order and conduct, models of the universe and other, moving metaphors and myths by means of study of the thoughts, acts, art, architecture, technology, literature, music and town
design of the West from the break-up of the Roman Empire until the Renaissance. Field trips to museums, concerts in Toronto, Detroit or Buffalo. Prereq: ARCH 143 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ARCH 247
courses.title: Renaissance to Revolution
paras: Sense of Periods and Styles

Analysis of the various styles emerging out of provincial and international Gothic, especially Italian use of classical modets, the spread of this ~ “renaissance” made, leading to consideration of the Mannerist, the Baroque, the Rococo, the Neoclassical; investigation of the course of men’s attitudes from humanism, nationalism, and Reformation through the Enlightenment until the French Revolution and Hume's dethronement of Reason. Field trips to museums, concerts in Toronto, Quebec, Detroit or Buffalo, Stratford Festival.
Prereq: ARCH 246 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ARCH 282
courses.title: Preservation Practice-Background
paras: An introduction to the field of preservation of older buildings, particularly in Canada; reference wil! be made to the philosophies and attitudes towards the preservation of older buildings and will be combined with the Study, in brief, of historical, social and architectural influences on Canadian building.

courses.label: ARCH 345
courses.title: Architectural Theory 1850-1940
paras: An introduction to the development of architectural theory from the mid-19th century to thé 2nd World War, through an examination of architectural movement and philosophies of the period and of the architecture, built and imagined, which they generated. Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 346
courses.title: Romanticism and 20th Century
paras: Sense of Periods and Styles

Depiction of “modern” culture as one in which the notion of environmental order as the fulfilling of natural law is replaced by a notion of order as the creation of the autonomous human wilis. Selected works in philosophy, - literature, art and architecture will be studied. an Prereq: ARCH 247 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ARCH 347
courses.title: The Roots of Civilization
paras: The course attempts to establish a basis for the understanding of the functions of myth, ceremony and ritual, the structures of primitive and ancient built environments, man’s attitude towards nature, and his use of the resource environment, the development of classical culture, and beginnings of science.
Prereq: ARCH 346 or consent of instructors.

paras: Architecture and urban design from the early fifteenth to the early seventeenth century in central and northern Italy. Special attention is paid to the development of theory and its relation to architectural practice. tn addition to the works of the major figures of the period. typical relationships between buildings and their urban and natural contexts are considered.
Prereq: ARCH 247 for architecture Students and consent of instructor for others.
Courses for Bachelor of Architecture

(For Recommended Program, see page 163). The courses for the Bachelor of Architecture Program are intended to prepare the student to demonstrate professional skill in separating, organizing, and conceptualizing actual problems in the man-made environment in his/her role as an architect, alone and in a team; to synthesize mechanical, structural and functional systems into architectural expressions which adapt to social needs and aspirations of society, user, client and community, atone and with the help of others; to adapt his/her skills to (a) real wortd constraints, (b) to the evolution of social economic and technologicat changes, and (c) to influence change both in constraints and environmental problems and know the current methods and procedures in professional practice for defining and solving environmental problems; to organize patterns of behaviour which assure continuing development for professional competence and relevance at all times; and to pass the examination for registration as an architect if he/she aspires to become a practising professional.

paras: The application of critica! thought will be exercised regularly through oral and written assignments on a wide range of designed human experiences; secondarily, there will be reading assignments to facilitate the practice of criticism through a broadening knowledge of critical theory and its relationship to culture.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ARCH 446
courses.title: Italian Urban History
paras: The course provides a survey of the history of settlement and urban form on the Italian penninsula from antiquity to the present day. In it the influences upon the structure of public and private space are outlined for each historical period. These include the constants such as geography and climate, but more especially the factors that induce and manifest change: politics, warfare, economics, social structure, the arts and theory.
Prereq: Registration in ARCH 492 or consent of instructor

paras: History of settlement and building in Rome and the surrounding area from antiquity to the present. Acts of design in architecture, urban form and landscape
related to political, cultural and spiritual
authority of Rome. Comparison drawn between the image of the city, represented in literature and art, and the material facts of the place. Field trips, lectures.

Introductory Notes

Courses designated “Arts’, those listed below, usually cover some topics and themes of general interest to several disciplines and their presentation is often made with this interdisciplinary perspective in view. Arts courses are elective courses in General and Honours programs and do not satisfy either the Group A or Group B requirements.

courses.label: ARTS 122
courses.title: Quest for Meaning In the 20th Century 1
paras: and 2

Against the background of rapidly shifting values in western culture, this course asks the student to examine his or her perspective and then face the resources of others in answering the question of Who am |? What is my obligation to society? What is my relationship to the natural world? ts there an ultimate meaning to life? Teaching methods inciude personal statements, thematic and biographical books and films.
Each term is unique. ARTS 122 is nota prerequisite for ARTS 123. Offered by Conrad Grebe! College.

courses.label: ARTS 198
courses.title: Introduction to Computer Technology
paras: A general introduction to the fundamental ideas of computers. Topics treated wilt include the use of an interactive computing system; word processing; and the beginnings of program writing. The course will examine the history of computing, and will consider the social and economic impact of the use of computers. No previous knowledge of computing is assumed.

courses.label: ARTS 202P
courses.title: Psychology of Religion in Historical Perspective
paras: A study of the Psychology of Religion in its historical perspective from the nineteenth century to the present day. Methods, techniques and practices of research that are applicable to the examination of religious experience will also be introduced.

courses.label: ARTS 211
courses.title: Computing Techniques in Language and Literature
paras: An introduction to non-mathematical computer programming, with special emphasis on the manipulation of language data. The programming language used will be PL/1. ARTS 211 will concentrate on gaining skill in computer programming. ARTS 212 will stress file management, advanced text formatting, and the use of system program utilities. Applications will include word indexes, text concordances, methods of computer-aided text comparison.
Prereq: ARTS 211 presupposes ARTS 198 or equivalent; 212 presupposes 211 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: ARTS 215
courses.title: Man In Crisis (Literary Views)
paras: A critical study of such themes as freedom vs. happiness, nihilism, collectivism vs. individualism, old tablets vs. utopias, alienation, earthbound fragmentation vs. the transcendentat in the artistic writings of Kafka, Brecht, Hesse, Nietzsche, Solzhenitsyn, Dostoevsky, Zamiatin, Camus, and others. Taught in English.

courses.label: ARTS 215A
courses.title: Man in Crisis 1 (Literary Views) Acritical study of Dostoevsky's The Grand Inquisitor, Nietzsche's Thus
paras: Spake Zarathustra, Tolstoy's What Men Live By, and works by Aldous Huxley, Zamiatin, Turgenev, and Andres. The two major themes are Utopia, the yearning for and the shape of perfectibility, and Nihilism, the denial and/or destruction of “Old Tablets” or “God is dead.”

courses.label: ARTS 215B
courses.title: Man in Crisis 2 (Literary Views)
paras: \ critical study of Brecht's The Jaucasian Chalk Circle, Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, and works by Ibsen, Hesse, Dostovevsky, Tolstoy, and 3olzhenitsyn. The two major themes are vihilism (see above) and Alienation, the divided self in exile, or the inability to give and to accept love.

paras: A study of the functional morphology of selected invertebrate types with special emphasis on the various grades of organization and development in the different phyla.

courses.label: BIOL 211
courses.title: Introductory Vertebrate Zoology
paras: An introduction to the structure, evolution and development of vertebrate organ systems.
Offered during the Spring term in oddnumbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 220
courses.title: Plant Blotogy 1 - The Living Plant
paras: An introduction to the structure, function and physiology of plants with emphasis on flowering plants.

courses.label: BIOL 221
courses.title: Plant Biology 2 - The Diversity of Plants
paras: A comparative survey of the morphology and life histories of the different kinds of plants and fungi important to man and an introduction to their evolution.
Offered during the Spring term in oddnumbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 222
courses.title: Non-Vascular Plants
paras: An introductory course which will survey the evolution, morphology.
ecology and importance to man of the fungi, algae, and bryophytes. 3y correspondence only for 1983-84.

courses.label: BIOL 230
courses.title: Introductory Cell Biology
paras: An introduction to the concepts of cell riology with emphasis on (i) the struc- .ural organization of the cell and its con- Stituent organelles and (ii) the function of critical molecular processes that are sharacteristic of living organisms.
When taking this course the lab must be designated separately. The fab is compulsory, but does not have any credit ‘weight.

Human Physiology
The physiology of the major organ systems including the nervous, mussular, circulatory, respiratory, urinary, digestive, endocrine and reproductive systems.
When taking this course the lab must be designated separately. The lab is comoulsory, but does not have any credit weight. Offered during the Spring term in even-numbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 239
courses.title: Genetics
paras: The mendelian basis of genetic analy- 3is. Chromosomal mechanisms in mitosis and meiosis. The origin, inheritance and adaptive significance of chromosomal changes. Nucleic acids as the carriers of genetic information. Natural selection and the evolution of genetic systems.
Offered during the Spring term in evennumbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 240
courses.title: Fundamentals of Microbiology
paras: Introduction to fundamental theories, principles and methods of microbiology. Structure, methods of cultivation, growth, effects of physical factors, and inhibition and killing of microorganisms will be studied.

courses.label: BIOL 241
courses.title: Introduction to the Microbial World
paras: Biological characterization of major bacterial groups, microorganisms as geochemical agents, utilization of microorganisms by man, and mechanisms of microbial pathogenicity.
Offered during the Spring term in oddnumbered years.

courses.label: BIOL 245
courses.title: General Microbiology 1
paras: History and scope of microbiology. Study of the characteristics of bacteria

courses.label: BIOL 246
courses.title: General Microbiology 2
paras: Relationships of microorganisms to man and his environment.
Prereq: BIOL 245
Open to students other than those intending to major in Biology or to enter the School of Optometry.

courses.label: BIOL 250
courses.title: Ecology
paras: An introduction to the study of the relationships of plants and animals to their environment. The nature of ecosystems, ecological energetics, biogeochemical cycling, community ecology, introduction to population biology. Field trips as required.

courses.label: BIOL 301
courses.title: Human Physiology
paras: The physiology of the major organ systems of the bady. The topics discussed include circulation, respiration, digestion and nutrition, metabolism, muscle, nervous system, special senses, and the endocrine system.
For Optometry students only.
BIOL31t W 2C,3L 05 Vertebrate Zoology
Major topics in vertebrate zoology as exemplified by both living and fossil members of the subphylum Craniata. Prereq: BIOL 211

courses.label: BIOL 315
courses.title: Invertebrate Zoology
paras: A survey of the major invertebrate phyla other than the arthropods, with emphasis on their functional anatomy, : classification and ways of life.
Prereq: BIOL 210

courses.label: BIOL 316
courses.title: Arthropod Zoology
paras: A survey of the phylum Arthropoda, including the insects, with emphasis on their classification, interrelationships and ways of life.
Prereq: BIOL 210

courses.label: BIOL 323
courses.title: Plant Anatomy and Morphogenesis
paras: Plant structure in relation to function and development with particular : reference to the vascular plants. Cell, tissue and organ differentiation. Prereq: BIOL 220 and 230

courses.label: BIOL 324
courses.title: The Flowering Plants
paras: A study of floral morphology in relation to classification and evolution. An introduction to taxonomy and nomenclature. History of taxonomy. Systems of classification. Mechanisms of pollination and dispersal.
Students entering this course are required to make a flowering plant collection. Instructions should be obtained from the Herbarium prior to the summer break.

courses.label: BIOL 327
courses.title: Mycology 1
paras: Fungal taxonomy and ecology; medical mycology; plant pathology; industrial applications; food and food processing; toxins and hallucinogens; biological control; fungi as coprophiles, predators, and symbionts with plants and animals. Prereq: BIOL 221

courses.label: BIOL 330
courses.title: Molecular Blology
paras: Molecular biological aspects of chromosome replication, expression of genetic information, functional translation of specific eukaryotic proteins, cell division, gamete formation, embryogenesis, hormone action, cellular interactions and cell differentiation.

courses.label: BIOL 331
courses.title: Cell Physiology
paras: The functional organization of cells with particular reference to cell-cell interaction, the structure, function and development of organelles and the biological roles of cellular membranes. Prereq: BIOL 230.

courses.label: BIOL 333
courses.title: Histology and Cytology
paras: The structure of mammalian cells, tis- Sues and organs interpreted in functional terms. Cell reproduction and differentiation, with some discussion of the embryological origin of tissues and the regulation of tissue growth. Light and electron microscopy techniques. Prereq: BIOL 271 or 230 or 233

courses.label: BIOL 335
courses.title: Plant Physiology
paras: A study of the principal physiological mechanisms that govern the water economy, mineral nutrition, transport processes and metabolism of plants.

courses.label: BIOL 336
courses.title: Embryology
paras: Fundamental processes and concepts in embryonic development including the acquisition of multicellularity, organi
zation of the early embryo, morphogenesis of tissues, major organ systems, fetal membranes, growth, differentiation and
analysis of common developmental defects.

courses.label: BIOL 337
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology 1
paras: The comparative physiology of animais with particular emphasis on homeostatic principles as demonstrated by water balance, excretion, nutrition, digestion and the endocrine system.

courses.label: BIOL 338
courses.title: Comparative Animal Physiology 2
paras: A comparative study of the cardiovas- - cular, nervous, muscular, respiratory and reproductive systems.

courses.label: BIOL 342
courses.title: Microbial Biotechnology
paras: The role of microorganisms in biotechnology. Topics examined will include the isolation, selection, and development of microorganisms important in biotechnology, and specialized techniques for their cultivation and maintenance. Processes studied will include biomass conversions, fermentations, bioproduction of compounds, nitrogen fixation, treatment and utilization of wastes and mineral leaching.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241 ar permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 344
courses.title: Microorganisms In Foods
paras: Food preservation, spoilage, poisoning and modern concepts in quality assurance programs are studied. The aim is to understand factors governing microbial changes in foods. Problem solving in the food industry is emphasized. Laboratory work will reflect current practices in quality control and testing. Prereq: BIOL 240-241 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 350
courses.title: Environmental Toxicology 1
paras: An introduction to the basic theories, principles and techniques of environmental toxicology. A comparative study of the effects of specific groups of toxicants on ecosystems; biodegradation and cycling.

courses.label: BIOL 356
courses.title: Population Ecology 1
paras: The ecology of populations. Topics include: demographic parameters and their estimation; population growth and regulation; competitive and predatorprey interactions; population genetics and evolution; applied population biology.
Prereq: BIOL 250 and STAT 202

courses.label: BIOL 416
courses.title: Entomology
paras: introduction to morphology, systematics and biology of insects. Brief field trips will be made to collect insects trom different local habitats.

courses.label: BIOL 420
courses.title: The Flora of Canada
paras: The composition and history of the Canadian flora. Major plant communities in Canada; their floristic composition and ecology. Endangered species and the conservation of our flora. Offered every other year. Alternates with BIOL 424.

courses.label: BIOL 424
courses.title: Ferns, Gymnosperms and Fern Allies
paras: an evolutionary survey

A detailed survey of the non-flowering vascular plants with emphasis on the extant members of each major group in Ontario. The phylogeny of the plants will be explored through a study of fossil ancestors in each line of evolution. Prereq: BIOL 220 and 221 or permission of the instructor. Offered every other year. Alternates with BIOL 420.

courses.label: BIOL 424B
courses.title: Phycology
paras: The taxonomy and ecology of freshwater and marine algae. Algal cytology, morphology, and life histories; biology of planktonic and attached algae; culturing of algae; experimental phycology; economic aspects of algae.
Prereq: BIOL 220 or 221

courses.label: BIOL 427
courses.title: Mycology 2
paras: The growth of mycological knowledge will be traced, and current developments analyzed. Extensive literature surveys, active class participation, and a lab project, will be required.
Prereq: BIOL 327

courses.label: BIOL 430
courses.title: Comparative Anima! Physiology 1
paras: A comparative study of respiratory, circulatory and endocrinological systems of animals: emphasis will be placed on invertebrate groups.

courses.label: BIOL 431
courses.title: Mammalian Reproductive Physiology
paras: A study of the endocrine and reproductive systems of mammals. Major topics include methods of hormone assay, chemistry of the hormones, regulation of secretion, mechanisms of hormone action, neurosecretion, reproductive cycles, gametogenesis and fertilization..

courses.label: BIOL 432
courses.title: Plant Growth and Development
paras: A study of the plant hormones and the mechanisms that control growth, dormancy and development.

courses.label: BIOL 434
courses.title: Advanced Genetics
paras: A detailed examination of the recent advances in molecular genetics with emphasis on the regulation of gene action in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Current research literature will be reviewed.
Offered every other yaar. Alternates with BIOL 438.

courses.label: BIOL 435
courses.title: Developmental Biology
paras: Analysis of embryonic development of selected organisms with emphasis on growth and the processes of subcellular, cellular and organ differentiation stressing recent experimental methodology.

courses.label: BIOL 438
courses.title: Advanced Molecular Biology
paras: An examination of the current major issues in molecular biology with emphasis on the technical and conceptual advances. Current research literature will be reviewed.
Prereq: BIOL 330. Offered every other year. Alternates with BIOL 434.

courses.label: BIOL 439
courses.title: Biochemistry of Natural Products
paras: The chemistry, functions and distribution of natural products including alkaloids, isoprenoids, amines, phenolics, cyanogenic glycosides and other important compounds in plants and other biological systems.
Prereq: At least one full-year course or equivalent in organic chemistry plus a one-term course in biochemistry that includes the essentials of carbohydrate and fat metabolism.

courses.label: BIOL 444
courses.title: Immunology
paras: Physical and biological properties of immunological agents that protect against disease, the procedures for their identification and their practical applications.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241

courses.label: BIOL 442
courses.title: Virology
paras: The nature of viruses and their interaction with their plant, microbial and animal hosts.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241

courses.label: BIOL 443
courses.title: Microorganisms of Industrial Importance
paras: A study of the role of microorganisms in industrial processes of biosynthesis and degradation.
Prereq: BIOL 344

courses.label: BIOL 444
courses.title: Microorganisms and Disease
paras: A study of the microorganisms involved in pathogenesis, their mode of infection, symptoms and prevention.
Prereq: BIOL 240, 241, 441

courses.label: BIOL 446
courses.title: Microbial Ecology
paras: Astudy of the ecological rotes of microorganisms. Examples from freshwater, terrestrial, marine and other ecosystems will be used to illustrate the activities and importance of microorganisms in these habitats.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241, or permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 447
courses.title: Environmental Microbiology
paras: A study of the environmental impact of microorganisms. Aspects of poilution, waste treatment, biodegradation of environmental contaminants, and nutrient cycling will be examined. Prereq: BIOL 240-241, 446 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 448
courses.title: Microbial Physiology 1
paras: A study of the physiology of microorganisms including multiphasic and synchronous growth, celi permeation, nutrition, physical and chemical environmental factors and metabolic mechanisms as elucidated by radioactively labelled tracers.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241, or permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 449
courses.title: Microbial Physiology 2
paras: A study of the physiology of microorganisms with emphasis on the metabolic mechanisms of fermentative microbes, cellular and sub-cellular protein synthesis including turnover of ribosomes, inhibition by antibiotics and the quantitative techniques used to elucidate the mechanisms of protein biosynthesis.
Prereq: BIOL 240-241; 448 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 450
courses.title: Aquatic Biology
paras: An introduction to the physics, chemistry and biology of the marine and freshwater environments.
Prereq: BIOL 315 or 316; 497
N.B. Limited to 24; priority will be given to Honours students.

courses.label: BIOL 452
courses.title: Introduction to Fisheries Biology
paras: The practices of fisheries biology; fish classification, life history, production, harvest and management.

courses.label: BIOL 455
courses.title: Environmental Toxicology 2
paras: Cellular, developmental and physiological effects of toxicants on multicellular organisms.
Prereq: BIOL 350

courses.label: BIOL 456
courses.title: Population Ecology 2
paras: The analysis of the structure and dynamics of plant and animal populations. Theoretical, mathematical and experimental approaches to the study of population ecology. Evolutionary
‘ processes in population biology.
Prereq: BIOL 356

courses.label: BIOL 457
courses.title: The Analysis of Communities
paras: Sampling procedures to estimate abundance and distribution of organisms in time and space. Methods to analyze succession. The classification and ordination of ecosystems. The response of ecosystems to exploitation. The role of biological management in conservation programs.
Prereq: BIOL 250 and STAT 202

courses.label: BIOL 468
courses.title: Quaternary Ecology
paras: A consideration of the Quaternary environment. Polien, plant macrofossil . and faunal remains as indicators of past environments. Relationship of fossil assemblages to modern ecosystems. Pollen analysis and the interpretation of fossit deposits.
Prereq: an introductory course in biology or geology, or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 460
courses.title: Statistical Procedures for Biologists 1
paras: An introduction to biometrical analysis. Measures of central tendency, dispersion and variability; the normal distribution; one-sample hypotheses; parametric and non-parametric twosample and paired-sample hypotheses.

correlation; goodness-of-fit tests; chisquare and G-tests for contingency tables; the Poisson and Binomial distributions. Throughout, the emphasis is on biological examples and problems from the student's own research area.

courses.label: BIOL 461
courses.title: Statistical Procedures for Biologists 2
paras: Design and analysis of experiments with an emphasis on the application of statistics to the student's area of research. Topics will inctude: analysis of variance; experimental designs; factorial experiments; models; missing data; transformations; a priori and a posteriori comparisons among means; regression analysis; analysis of covariance.

courses.label: BIOL 473
courses.title: Blosystematics and Evolution
paras: A study of the processes of evolution: the differentiation of populations and the origin of new forms of life. Prereq: BIOL 239

courses.label: BIOL 474
courses.title: History of Blology
paras: The development of biological thought from Greek and Roman times to the present; i.e. from classification to the present experimental approach.
Not to be taken in conjunction with SCI 400.

courses.label: BIOL 480
courses.title: Biotechnology
paras: Biotechnology is an interdisciplinary science which entails understanding how biological processes can be developed for large scale practical use. The topics examined include (1) genetic engineering (2) enzymes for industrlai and pharmaceutical use and (3) plant and animal cell culture systems. Prereq: BIOL 240-241 and CHEM 237 or permission of the instructor.

courses.label: BIOL 497
courses.title: Field Course 1
paras: This intensive field course of two weeks duration may be one of several arranged or approved by the Department and is usually taken after completion of third year.

courses.label: BIOL 498
courses.title: Field Course 2
paras: Required of all honours biologists except those who take BIOL 497. This general interest field course usually of one week duration may be one of several arranged or approved by the Department and is usually taken after completion of third year.

courses.label: BIOL 499
courses.title: Senior Honours Project
paras: A senior-year research project. Normally, only students attaining a 70% cumulative major average will be accepted into this course. Students are referred to the co-ordinator for BIOL 499 for further details.

Course Descriptions
Introductory Notes

The core courses for each year of the program constitute an interdisciplinary study of Canadian problems, and are offered either in a lecture/tutorial format or a seminar format (depending on the number of students registered). These courses are given by faculty members of the participating departments of the University and by eminent scholars
from other parts of Canada who visit the University for brief or extended periods during the year.
Canadian Studies content courses in various disciplines are listed in Chapter 15.
Core Courses

courses.label: CDNST 101
courses.title: Landforms and Mindscapes
paras: An introduction to the Canadian landscape and its early impact upon the creative imagination of Canadians. The course sets out to provide a basis for dealing with contemporary Canadian culture.

courses.label: CDNST 201
courses.title: Sociat Regionalism
paras: Lecturers in Geography, Political Science, Sociology and History discuss the roles which economic disparities, social elites, federal/provincial relations and politica! parties play in defining Canadian regionatism. Particular attention is paid to Quebec's desire for separate status.

courses.label: CDNST 202
courses.title: - Cultural Regionalism
paras: Lecturers discuss the contribution made by literature, film, drama, and fine arts in defining distinctive regional identities in Canada. Particular attention is paid to the emergence of a distinctive Ontario culture.

courses.label: CDNST 301
courses.title: Regionalism: West
paras: This course continues the exploration of Canadian regionalism by applying knowledge gained in CON ST 201/202 to distinctive problems of the Canadian west and northwest. The focus of the seminar will vary according to the interests of the faculty and students. Prereq: CON ST 101, 201 or 202 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CDNST 302
courses.title: Regionalism: East
paras: This course continues the exploration of Canadian regionalism by applying knowledge gained in CON ST 201/202 to distinctive problems of Atlantic Canada. The focus of the seminar will . vary according to the interests of the faculty and students.
Prereq: CON ST 101, 201 or 202 or permission of instructor

courses.label: CDNST 400
courses.title: Research Essay
paras: An extensive senior research essay, supervised by a.committee composed of faculty members from two or more of the participating departments, which deals with a specific aspect of Canada utilizing material and methods from several different disciplines.
Prereq: CON ST 301/302

Course Descriptions
introductory Notes
Students whose registration in first year was prior to September 1979 fallow a program described in the 1980/81 Calendar..
Prerequisite: For all courses in the | Department of Chemical Engineering, registration in the Department or permission of the Associate Chairman {Undergraduate Studies) is a requirement.

courses.label: CHE 100
paras: F 3C,1T,6L for first 6 weeks 0.75 Chemical Engineering Concepts 1
An introduction to the basic methods
and principles used by engineers in the analysis and design of physical processes: units, dimensions, and measure-- _ ments; mass balances; behaviour of
fluids. Laboratory on visual communication is included.

courses.label: CHE 101
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Concepts 2
paras: An extension of the topics covered in CH E 100; energy balances; laboratory experiments illustrate the physical principles discussed.

courses.label: CHE 102
courses.title: Chemistry for Engineers
paras: Chemical principles with applications in engineering. Stoichiometric calculations, properties of gases, properties of liquids and solutions; gas phase chemical equilibrium, ionic equilibrium in aqueous solution, oxidation-reduction reactions, chemical kinetics.

courses.label: CHE 210
courses.title: Transport Processes 1 (Equilibrium Stage Operations)
paras: Equilibrium between phases; the equilibrium-stage concept. Cascades of stages with and without reflux; examples of their analysis when used to separate components by distillation, extraction, absorption and leaching. Introduction to computer methods for multicomponent mixtures.

courses.label: CHE 213
courses.title: Transport Pr 2 (Fluid Mechanics)
paras: Fundamentals of fluid flow; conservation laws for mass, momentum and mechanical energy; flow of fluid in conduits; flow past immersed bodies. Description, collection and separation of particulate systems.

courses.label: CHE 220
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 1
paras: Basic concepts of probability and their relevance to engineering decisions. Statistical frequency distributions, tests of significance, correlations, curve fitting, sampling theory, applications: errors, design of experiments.

courses.label: CHE 230
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 1
paras: Introduction te physical chemistry. Ideal and real gases, the kinetic theory of gases, first law of thermodynamics, thermochemistry, heats of reaction, second law, chemical equilibria in simple systems, phase equilibria in simple systems, third law.
CHE231S,F 3C,1T 0.5
Physical Chemistry 2

Thermodynamics of systems of variable composition; properties of solutions, ideal solutions, colligative properties of solutions, phase equilibria in complex systems, non-ideal solutions. Surface phenomena. Chemical kinetics; empirical laws and mechanisms. Prereg: CH E 230

courses.label: CHE 232
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry 1
paras: Wave mechanics, atomic structure and the periodic table, chemical bonding, structural chemistry of elements and compounds, introductory transition metal chemistry, some thermodynamic aspects of inorganic chemistry.

courses.label: CHE 233
courses.title: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
paras: Experiments on viscosity of gases and liquids, chemical kinetics, absorption, homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, thermochemistry, phase equilibria, diffusion, determination of molecular weight of polymers, training in technical report writing.

courses.label: CHE 314
courses.title: Transport Processes 3 (Heat Transfer)
paras: introduction to heat transfer, momentum-heat transfer analogies and dimensional analysis, steady and transient heat conduction, convection and applications to engineering problems, radiant heat transfer and heat transfer with change of phase.
Prereq: CH E 213

courses.label: CHE 317
courses.title: Transport Processes 4 (Mass Transfer)
paras: Mass transfer by molecular and turbulent motion, heat-mass transfer analogies, mass transfer models and application to separations such as: distillation, absorption, adsorption, extraction etc.; simultaneous heat and mass transfer in gas-liquid contacting and solids drying; introduction to mass transfer with chemical reaction. Prereq: CHE 314

courses.label: CHE 320
courses.title: Applied Mathematics 2
paras: Gamma-Beta- and error-functions; sinecosine-, exponential- and ellipticintegrals, linear differential equations; Wronskian, Green function; initial and boundary value problems; Bessel functions; Fourier series, integrals and transforms; orthogonal functions: Laplace transforms; applications.
Course Descriptions . Chemical Engineering

courses.label: CHE 321
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control 1
paras: Block and signal flow diagrams, proportional-integral-derivative controllers, frequency response techniques, analytical and graphical stability criteria. Introduction to modern control theory. Prereq: MATH 216, CH E 314, CH E 320

courses.label: CHE 330
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
paras: Thermodynamics of flow processes, vapour power plants, internal combustion engines, liquefaction of gases, refrigeration and evaporation, chemical equilibria in chemical reactions, thermal pollution, the energy crisis, efficient energy utilization and thermodynamics. Prereq: CH E 231

courses.label: CHE 331
courses.title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
paras: Homogeneous reactors; batch, CSTR, tubular flow systems, ideal models, residence time distributions in ideal reactors, temperature effects, steady states, semi-batch systems, nonideal behaviour. Heterogeneous catalysis; mass transfer effects; catalytic rate equations, fixed and fluidized bed reactors. Prereq: CH E 231

courses.label: CHE 332
courses.title: Inorganic Chemistry 2
paras: Introductory electrochemistry; electrolysis, electrolytic conductance and transport, reversible electrode processes, irreversible electrode processes and electrode kinetics, electrochemical measurements and their analytical applications, chemistry of corrosion. Prereq: CH E 232

courses.label: CHE 333
courses.title: Instrumental Methods of Chemical Analysis
paras: An introduction to modern analysis including optical, electrochemical, radio-chemical, chromatographic and spectroscopic methods.

courses.label: CHE 382
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 1
paras: Mathematics of annuities, mortgages, bonds and small loans: cost accounting, including direct costing, depreciation, taxes and financial statements. Sizing and costing of piping and heat transfer equipment; design of process components.

courses.label: CHE 410
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Laboratory
paras: Experimental applications of physical and chemical principles using pilot scale equipment, experiments illustrating major unit operations (distillation, absorption, extraction, drying, humidification).
Prereq: CH E 314

courses.label: CHE 484
courses.title: Engineering Economics and Process Design 2
paras: Estimation of sales, and capital and operating costs of a new process or products; study of criteria for the appraisal of capital and expenditures; critical path methods; linear programming. Sizing and costing of mass transfer and other process equipment; design of processes.

courses.label: CHE 486
courses.title: Technical Seminar
paras: Each student will be expected to prepare and deliver a seminar on material from the recent literature or industrial experience, as well as an impromptu talk on a variety of topics. This course is graded CR or NCR, and CR must be obtained as a requirement for graduation.

courses.label: CHE 501
courses.title: The Engineer as Entrepreneur
paras: A survey course covering the place of small business in Canadian manufacturing. The rote of innovation in organizing a successful new business. Topics important to business startup: patents, business plans, financing new ventures, bookkeeping, marketing, government assistance, taxation, and bankruptcy.

courses.label: CHE 502
courses.title: Fundamentals of Petroleum Production
paras: Background for understanding the physical principles involved and the terminology used in petroleum production. Fundamentals of surface chemistry (capillarity), characterization of and fluid flow through porous media. Principles of production performance, water flooding and enhanced recovery techniques.

courses.label: CHE 510
courses.title: Prediction of Physico-chemical Properties
paras: Methods of estimating physicochemical properties of gases and liquids in cases where experimental values are absent. Prediction is usually based on correlations of a form suggested in part by theory, with empirical constants based on experimental data.

courses.label: CHE 515
courses.title: Two-Phase Flow Operations
paras: Introductory theory of one-dimensional two-phase flow: conventions, definitions, homogeneous theory, separated flow (Lockhart-Martinelli), particulate characterization and behaviour; applications: two-phase fiow in pipes, boiling and evaporation, filtration.

courses.label: CHE 517
courses.title: Performance of Separation Processes
paras: Introduction, patterns of change and computational approaches. group methods, limited flows and stage requirements, capacity and efficiency of contacting devices, energy requirements, selection, optimal design and operation, mass transfer with chemical reaction.

courses.label: CHE 520
courses.title: Chemical Engineering Analysis
paras: Application of advanced mathematical techniques to the analysis of chemical engineering processes.
Prereq: Permission of instructor

courses.label: CHE 521
courses.title: Process Dynamics and Control 2
paras: Analog computation, time domain analysis, control of complex chemical systems.
Prereq: CH E 420

courses.label: CHE 523
courses.title: Process Control Laboratory
paras: Experiments on process dynamics, control and analog simulation of chemical processes. Time constant, step and frequency response, controller settings, cascade contro! of thermal, tiquid level, and reaction systems. Prereq: CH E 420

courses.label: CHE 540
courses.title: Introduction to Polymer Science
paras: Basic concepts of polymer chemistry, classification of polymers, introductory physical chemistry of polymers, organic
chemistry of polymerization reactions of —
polymers, naturally occuring polymers.

courses.label: CHE 541
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymers
paras: Polymer solutions, molecular characterization of polymers, molecular weight distributions, morphology and crystallinity in polymers, reaction kinetics and mechanism of addition and condensation polymerization.
Prereq: CH E 540
CHES43 W 3L 05
Polymer Laboratory
Experimental studies of polymerization and physical properties of polymers.
Course Descriptions . 293 Chemical Engineering
condensation and addition polymerization, copolymerization, molecular weight, extrusion rheology.
Coreq: CH E 541

courses.label: CHE 550
courses.title: Introduction to Extractive Metallurgy
paras: Physical and chemical nature of ores and intermediates, introductory pyrometaliurgy, hydrometallurgy and electrometailury, survey of extraction processes, application of the principles of thermodynamics and kinetics to
metallurgical processes.

courses.label: CHE 551
courses.title: Metallurical Chemistry
paras: lonic equilibria, thermodynamics and kinetics of reactions in solution, bonding, stability and stereochemistry of co-ordination compounds and mechanisms of their reaction, introductory hydrometallurgy, corrosion and homogeneous Catalysis.

courses.label: CHE 553
courses.title: Principtes of High Temperature Extractive Metallurgy
paras: In-depth discussion of several processes of importance in Canada: blastfurnace smelting (iron, lead, zinc), steel making and other specialized refining Processes, pyrometaiiurgical treatment of sulfide ores, and fused salt electrolysis. The emphasis is on the interplay of the underlying thermodynamic, kinetic, transport, and processengineering considerations.

courses.label: CHE 560
courses.title: Introduction to Biochemical
paras: Engineering .

Aspects of the life sciences of interest to the biochemical industries and to environmental pollution. Classification and growth characteristics of microorganisms. Physico-chemical properties of biological compounds. Metabolism and biochemical kinetics. Course includes some lab work.

courses.label: CHE 561
courses.title: Fermentation Operations
paras: Application of process engineering principles to the design and operation of fermentation reactors which are widely used in the pharmaceutical, food, brewing, and waste treatment industries. Aspects of mass transfer, heat transfer, mixing, and rheology with biochemical and biological constraints. Course includes some lab work. Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: CHE 563
courses.title: Food Processing
paras: Applications of unsteady and steady state heat and/or mass transfer operations to processing natural and texturized foods. Design and analysis of sterilization, low temperature preservation, concentration, separation and purification processes. Effects of formulation, additives, and processing on organoleptic and ‘nutritional quality. Prereq: CH E 560 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: CHE 570
courses.title: Alr Poltution
paras: Treatment of gaseous waste products from representative Canadian industries; characterization and toxicity of filtration, scrubbing, cycloning, electrostatic precipitation, and other chemical treatment, legal, socio-political, economic and engineering aspects.
CHES71 W 3C 05
Water Pollution

Treatment of waste water from metals processing industries; waste characterization; toxicity; recycling; treatment by electro-oxidation/reduction, ion exchange, solvent extraction, absorption, electrodiatysis, reverse osmosis, etc.; economics, regulations, moral, legal, social and political implications.

courses.label: CHE 580
courses.title: Research-Design Project 1
paras: individually supervised research and/or design project on any Chemical Engineering subject chosen by the studentprofessor group. Written report required.

courses.label: CHE 581
courses.title: Research-Design Project 2 Continuation of CH E 580
paras: Equivalent to two one-term courses. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 583
courses.title: Process System Design
paras: The undergraduate curriculum is brought together to accomplish, by team effort, the basic objective of the process engineer: the design of an integrated process. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, and a public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 585
courses.title: Technical Elective Project
paras: An individually supervised research or design project, based on one of the technical elective courses taken in the 4A term. A written report, meeting minimum technical report standards, anda public oral presentation will be required.

courses.label: CHE 007
courses.title: General Awareness Seminar
paras: Informal discussions on the Chemical Engineering program.

Some courses are regularly given every other year, and are listed In their regular places. Any other courses not offered in the current academic year are listed at the end of this section.
introductory Notes

In all cases, it is the student's responsibility to determine eligibility to enter a course. It is advisable to obtain special consents in writing before registration period to avoid delays and complications.
Most 300- and 400-level courses are listed as 2 lecture hours. An additional hour may be scheduled at the discretion of the lecturer, usually for a tutorial.

Included are forhhulae, nomenclature, stoichiometry, an introduction to thermochemistry, solution chemistry, chemical equilibria, acids, bases, oxidation-reduction reactions, kinetics and bonding. Successful completion of this course fulfills the University Admission requirements where high school chemistry is necessary. No University credit. Offered by correspondence only.

paras: Classical and wave theories of the electronic structure of atoms. The periodic table. Formation and characteristics of ionic and covalent bonds. Molecular orbital and valence bond theories. Bonding in molecular, ionic, and metallic solids. Structure and stereochemistry of simple inorganic compounds.
Prereq: Grade 13 Chemistry, Physics Antireq: CHEM 218

paras: Current models of bonding in tnorganic Chemistry. Prediction of stereochemistry and electronic structure. Inorganic nomenclature.

courses.title: Chemistry of Non-Transition Elements
paras: Group trends in main group chemistry. Emphasis will be placed on correlation of structure with physical properties in various groups of compounds. Prereq: CHEM 212 or 218 Antireg: CHEM 313

- logy students, with related experiments.

Prereq: CHEM 264 or 266

courses.label: CHEM 237L
courses.title: Introductory Blochemistry Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments for students taking CHEM 237.

courses.label: CHEM 254
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 1
paras: This course emphasizes the macroscopic approach. Areas to be studied include properties of gases: the first,’ second and third laws of thermodynamics applied to ideal systems; chemical equilibrium.
Prereq: CHEM 123, MATH 113a/b or equivalent.

courses.label: CHEM 255
courses.title: Physical Chemistry 2

The difterence between thermodynamic and dynamic equilibria is introduced to deal with rates of chemical reactions and their relationship to experimental data. Prereq: CHEM 254

Prereq: CHEM 124

Prereq: CHEM 264 taken in or after 1981-82

courses.label: CHEM 353

paras: Basic definitions and polymer nomenclature, molecular weight averages and distributions, polymer stereochemistry, step-growth and chain-growth polymerization reactions, applications of polymers.

courses.label: CHEM 355L

paras: An introductory survey of the thermodynamics of ideal systems; the application of thermodynamic principles to the study of solution, phase equilibria, chemical equilibrium and the properties of electrolytes.

courses.label: CHEM 416
courses.title: Applied Inorganic Chemistry

courses.label: CHEM 417

courses.title: Bioorganic Mechanisms
paras: Modern techniques of biosynthetic studies. Enzyme reaction mechanisms. Prereq: CHEM 237 and one of 368, 366, 365.

courses.label: CHEM 452
courses.title: Colloids, Liquid Crystals and Bilayer Chemistry
paras: The colloidal size range, the importance of the interface, classical studies on Brownian motion, light scattering, the micelle formation of detergents in water and solubilisation. Phase diagrams of soaps and lipids and their study by X- ray diffraction and NMR. The biological membrane as an entity of colloidal size. The related spectroscopy, microscopy, atc. of lyotropic liquid crystais and bilayers.
Prereq: CHEM 255

courses.label: CHEM 453
courses.title: Polymer Properties and Polymerization
paras: Copolymerization, emulsion polymerization, ionic and coordinate polymerization, basics of polymerization process selection. Prereq: CHEM 353 or equivalent.

courses.label: CHEM 454
courses.title: Surface Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the physical chemistry of surfaces. Qualitative and quantitative descriptions of surfaces and interfaces and the development of relevant techniques and theories. Application to surface tension, spreading, wetting, adsorption, and other interfacial phenomena.
Prereq: CHEM 255

courses.label: CHEM 455
courses.title: Electrochemistry
paras: Electrolytic conductance and transport, thermodynamics of electrolytic cells. Reversible and irreversible electrode processes, metallic corrosion; study of selected industrial electrochemical processes.
Prereq: CHEM 254 or 356

courses.label: CHEM 456
courses.title: Catalysis
paras: An introduction to heterogeneous catalysis. Examination of the physical manifestations of catalysis and the development of experimental techniques and theoretical methods for the measurement and elucidation of catalytic phenomena.
Prereq: CHEM 255

courses.label: CHEM 457
courses.title: Experimental Aspects of Polymer Science
paras: Selected experiments to illustrate polymerization, polymer properties and fabrication processes.
Prereq: CHEM 353 or equivalent Antireq: CH E 543

courses.label: CHEM 458
courses.title: Quantum Chemistry
paras: The nature of electronic structure and chemical bonding in H; and other
Simple molecules and its implications
for theories of chemical reactions. Prereq: Chem 355

courses.label: CHEM 464
courses.title: Spectroscopy in Organic Chemistry
paras: Elucidation and identification of organic structures by contemporary spectroscopic techniques.
Prereq: CHEM 265 or 364

courses.label: CHEM 465
courses.title: Special Topics in Organic Chemistry
paras: Topics will be selected from photochemistry. organometiallics, synthesis, heterocyclics, natural products, molecular rearrangements. (May be taken in third and fourth year as 465A and 465B provided topics are different).
Prereq or coreq: CHEM 365 or 368

courses.label: CHEM 492
courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
paras: Laboratory work on a senior year research project. See CHEM 492 coordinator for descriptive booklet and details.
