paras: ENGL 151

courses.label: ENGL 109
courses.title: Introduction to Essay Writing 1
paras: The course teaches the construction of the expository essay with attention to the structure of good paragraphs, to techniques of putting the essay together, and to the nature of the language. Ten to twelve short writing assignments are required.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
Note: Students may receive credit for only one of ENGL 109 and ENGL 129R.

courses.label: ENGL 110
courses.title: Introduction to Essay Writing 2
paras: The course teaches the construction of the persuasive essay, with attention to the elements of logical thinking, to the techniques of successful persuasion, and to the demands of the library research paper. Six to eight writing assignments are required.
Prereq: ENGL 109

courses.label: ENGL 129R
courses.title: Introduction to Written English
paras: Instruction provided in basic grammar, sentence and paragraph structure, elements of composition and essay writing including focus on theme, development of central idea, exposition and argumentation. Minimum of four hours of instruction each week with additional tutorial hours as required. Prereq: Open only to students whose maternal language is not English and who lack language mastery sufficient for admission to other introductory English language courses.
Course Descriptions
English

courses.label: ENGL 209
courses.title: Advanced Essay Writing
paras: Provides further opportunities for serious students of writing to study and to practise descriptive, expository, argumentative, and persuasive writing. In addition to lectures, there are workshop sessions in which student writing is discussed.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above.

courses.label: ENGL 210
courses.title: Report Writing
paras: The many functions of the report - an orderly and objective communication of factual information which serves some specific purpose - are taught. Students will receive practice in research, in organization, and in writing many kinds of reports.
Prereq: Second-year standing or above.

courses.label: ENGL 335
courses.title: Creative Writing
paras: Aimed at encouraging students to develop their creative and critical
potentiais, the course consists of
supervised practice, tutorials, and seminar discussions.

courses.label: ENGL 150
courses.title: English as an Instrument of Thought and Communication 1
paras: The course is designed to improve the reading and writing of students from al! disciplines. In order to develop clarity of thought and critical awareness, students will identify and study in several media the various ends that are served by language: objective reporting; persuasion; argument; and emotional, social, and artistic expression. About eight written exercises are assigned.

courses.label: ENGL 151
courses.title: English as an Instrument of Thought and Communication 2
paras: A continuation of ENGL 150. From a basis of simple semantics and elementary logic, students wilt proceed to examine more complex language in fiction and other forms of literature. About six written exercises are assigned.
Prereq: ENGL 150. °

courses.label: ENGL 140R
courses.title: The Use of English.1
paras: The use and abuse of spoken and written English. The study and evaluation of language as it is used for various purposes (e.g. colloquial, scientific, legal, potitical, commercial, journalistic, literary) in order to increase critical awareness and to help students to write clearly and effectively.

courses.label: ENGL 141R
courses.title: The Use of English 2
paras: Acontinuation of ENGL 140R. The
study of factual, emotive, scientific and imaginative writing; relevance, context; meaning, tone, feeling and intention. Prereq: ENGL 140R.

courses.label: ENGL 240R
courses.title: Form and Function 1
paras: The uses of literacy and the functions of language as acquired in ENGL 140R/141R. These will be applied to the more advanced form of the literary and critical assignment essay, involving comparison, evaluation and exposition.
Group Two
Courses in this group carry degree credit and may be counted as fulfilling the minimum requirements for a General or Honours program in Engfish.

courses.label: ENGL 102
courses.title: The Major Forms of Literature
paras: Different kinds of literature will be explored so as to discover how the shape of a literary work contributes to its meaning. Students will read ballad, lyric, and narrative poetry; classic tragedy and comedy and absurdist, existential and expressionist plays; novels and short stories.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Nature and Structure of the Engtish Language
paras: Introduction to the study of the English language. Topics to be discussed include the nature and origin of language, the structure of English and its development, and the relations between language and reality.

courses.label: ENGL 103B
courses.title: Varieties of English
paras: introduction to the study of varieties of the English language - regional, social, temporal, functional, and stylistic. The
relations of languages and literature and of speech and writing will be discussed.
Prereq: ENGL 103A or consent of instructor.
ENGL 105A/B
A close examination of a representative selection of works by major British, Canadian, American and other authors writing in English.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 105A
courses.title: Twentieth-Century Literature in English
paras: A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as W.B. Yeats, Virginia Woolf, D.H. Lawrence, T.S. Eliot, and Ernest Hemingway.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 105B
courses.title: Twentieth-Century Literature in English
paras: A continuation of ENGL 105A. A close examination of a representative selection of works by major authors writing in English such as William Fautkner, Dylan Thomas, and Margaret Laurence. Prereq: ENGL 105A or consent of instructor. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 108
courses.title: Themes of Literature
paras: An exploration of the great variety of literature through thematic perspectives.

courses.label: ENGL 108A
courses.title: The Hero
paras: A study of human excellence in thought and action embodied in representative men and women, as seen through works of literature.

courses.label: ENGL 108C
courses.title: Literature and Morality
paras: Works in English literature from its beginnings are selected for their bearings on questions of morality.

courses.label: ENGL 108E
courses.title: Women in Literature
paras: A study of the nature and role of women in British, Canadian, and American literature. Works by both men and women will be studied in which women are seen in such forms as mothers, saints, sex objects, and witches.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
Course Descriptions 319
English

courses.label: ENGL 108F
courses.title: The Rebel
paras: A sutdy of various works of literature in which the protagonist is a rebel against existing norms. The course will examine a number of rebel types and concepts, moral implications and final outcomes either in successful realization or in tragic defeat.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 108H
courses.title: Tsolation and Alienati
paras: The study of a variety of works centering on the theme of man in crisis, the stress being on the individual at variance with his inner self, his fellow man, or his world. The course will discuss the process in which wisdom and maturity are gained as the ultimate products of suffering.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 190
courses.title: Shakespeare
paras: Designed for students in all faculties, the course examines some of Shakespeare's comedies, history plays, and tragedies. Shakespeare's variety and flexibility in developing characters and dramatic structures are stressed, as are significant themes.
No previous work in Shakespeare is required.
ENGL 200A/B
Survey of British Literature
An historical survey of major figures, types and trends in British literature from the Middle Ages to the present. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 200A
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 1
paras: An historical survey of major figures, types and trends in British literature from the Middle Ages to the late eighteenth century.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 200B
courses.title: Survey of British Literature 2
paras: An historical survey of major figures, types and trends in British titerature from the late eighteenth century to the present. —
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 201
courses.title: The Short Story
paras: This course deals with the history, and techniques of the short story with emphasis upon works by such British, American-and Canadian writers as
Henry James, James Joyce, D.H. Lawrence, Ernest Hemingway, and Alice Munro.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 202A/B
The Bible and Literature
The study of major themes, stories, myths, and characters of the Old and New Testaments of the King James Bible, and their inftuence on other English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 202A
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 1
paras: Selections from Hebrew Scripture will be studied in relation to English literature.

courses.label: ENGL 202B
courses.title: The Bible and Literature 2
paras: The course will continue the study of the Bible, emphasizing the Christian gospels and epistles in relation to English literature.
Prereq: ENGL 202A or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENGL 205R
courses.title: The Canadian Short Story
paras: The Canadian short story, from its beginnings - in the bush, in the north, on the land, in the small towns - through the struggles of an urbanizing society to the present. Students will be expected to work in some depth with individual authors.

courses.label: ENGL 208A
courses.title: Forms of Fantasy
paras: This course will deal with the history and forms of fantasy written for adults. In considering the genre, related forms like the romance, the fairy tale, the fable, and the gothic horror story will be discussed. Authors such as Morris, C.S. Lewis, Tolkien, Williams, and White will. be studied.

courses.label: ENGL 208B
courses.title: Science Fiction
paras: Various examples drawn, for instance, from Utopian and anti-Utopian science fiction, social science fiction, “gadget” science fiction, parapsychology, and alternate worlds and beings, will be considered. Some attention will be given to the historical development of the genre.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208C
courses.title: Studies in Children’s Literature
paras: This course will deal with classic works of children’s literature, including fantasy written primarily for children. Selections from such authors as Kipling, Woolf, C.S. Lewis, George MacDonald, Kenneth Grahame, and Thurber will be studied.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208E
courses.title: Women Writers of the 20th Century
paras: A study of such major 20th-century women writers as Woolf, Hellman, Murdoch, McCarthy, Lessing, Laurence, Plath and Atwood. Emphasis will be on the concerns of these writers with the roles of women, the writer's search for new meanings, and their innovations in literary forms.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 208H
courses.title: Arthurian Legend
paras: The story of Arthur and his knights of the Round Table will be discussed as it is treated at various times in various works and genres. Such matters will be considered as the character of Arthur, the concept of Camelot, and the Fellowship of the Round Tabie.

courses.label: ENGL 208K
courses.title: Detective Fiction
paras: The history and characteristics of the “detective novel,” the “novel of crime,” and the “thriller.” Attention will also be given to the novel of intrigue and espionage. Such authors as Poe, Collins, Doyle, Chesterton, Hammett, Buchan, Greene, Deighton, and Le Carre will be discussed. The course includes the examination of critical approaches to the form of detective fiction.

courses.label: ENGL 208Q
courses.title: Ordered Chaos: The Apocalyptic Vision in Literature
paras: A study of dehumanized worlds in fiction that can be called “apocalyptic”. Works by such writers as St. John the Divine, Shakespeare, Mary Shelley, Aldous Huxley, Mordecai Richler, and Kurt Vonnegut will be studied.

courses.label: ENGL 211
courses.title: The Novel
paras: The novel, by its nature, constitutes an attempt to formulate and to interpret the bewildering human experience. This course undertakes an exploration of the forms that attempt can take. British.
Course Descriptions
English
Canadian, and American novels will be studied. The two halves of the course may be taken independently.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 211
courses.title: The Novel 1
paras: A study of the novel in English from its beginnings to the late 19th century.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 212
courses.title: The Novel 2
paras: A study of the novel in English from the fate 19th century to the present.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 214
courses.title: Themes in Canadian Literature
paras: The course will survey a theme which is significant to the understanding of the Canadian literary mind. Topics will vary from section to section.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.
ENGL 2514/B

The Practice and Theory of Criticism The study and practice of skills needed for a close, analytical reading of literary texts and for the writing of critical analyses on them; studies of theories concerning literature and literary criticism.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 251A
courses.title: The Practice and Theory of Criticism 1
paras: The first half of ENGL 2514/8 (see above)
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 251B
courses.title: The Practice and Theory of Criticism 2
paras: The continuation of ENGL 251A (see above).
Prereq: ENGL 251A
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 305A/B
Old English
An introduction to the English language in its earliest form and to the literature of pre-Conquest Engiand.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 305A
courses.title: Old English 1
paras: An introduction to the English language in its earliest form and to English prose in pre-Conquest England, examining Old English prose style, its principal practitioners and their world view.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 305B
courses.title: Old English 2
paras: An introduction to Old English poetry, noting in representative Old English poems those things about its purpose, style, and its audience which make it unique but which also provide the beginnings of the English poetic tradition.
Prereq: ENGL 305A
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 310A4/B
Middle English
A study of Middle English literature with special emphasis on the work of Geoffrey Chaucer.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 310A
courses.title: Middle English 1
paras: A study of the minor poems of Chaucer, “The Book of the Duchess”, “Parliament of Fowts”, and “Troilus”, along with related Middle English texts.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 310B
courses.title: Middle English 2 A study of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales
paras: _and related Middle English poems and
prose. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 312
courses.title: Literature of the Commonweatth
paras: A survey of Australian poetry and prose, with some consideration of the literatures, in English, from Africa and the West Indies.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 313
courses.title: Canadian Literature to 1920
paras: A study of Canadian prose and verse to 1920, with particular attention to the poetry of the School of the Sixties and to the historical and idyllic novels of the 19th and early 20th centuries.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 314
courses.title: Canadian Poetry Since 1920
paras: Poetry in Canada from E.J. Pratt and A.J.M. Smith to Leonard Cohen. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 315
courses.title: Canadian Prose Since 1920
paras: The Canadian novel since the appearance of Morley Callaghan, with brief consideration of the essay and short story during the period.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 3304/8
Elizabethan Literature (excluding Drama)

A study of the principal writers of prose and of lyric and narrative poetry in England during and immediately before the reign of Elizabeth |. Reserved for special attention is Spenser's epic poem glorifying Elizabeth | and England - The Faerie Queene.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 330A
courses.title: Elizabethan Literature 1 (excluding Drama)
paras: A study of the principal writers of prose and of lyric and narrative poetry in England during and immediately before the reign of Elizabeth |.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 330B
courses.title: Elizabethan Literature 2 (excluding Drama)
paras: The continuation of ENGL 330A. Reserved for special attention is Spenser's epic poem glorifying England and Elizabeth | - The Faerie Queene. Prereq: ENGL 330A or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 343
courses.title: American Literature
paras: The meaning of America - the myth, the dream, and the reality - as experienced through its major literary works. Sin, guilt, madness, mysticism, and grace: the search for fulfillment and peace by such writers as Poe, Thoreau, Whitman, Twain, and Crane.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 344
courses.title: Modern American Literature
paras: Approaches to reality amid the confusion and uncertainty of 20th-century America. Emphasis on such major writers as Faulkner, Miller, and Cummings.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 345
courses.title: Studies in American Literature
paras: (Usually only one or two courses from this series are offered each year.)
Course Descriptions 321
English

courses.label: ENGL 345B
courses.title: American Fiction
paras: The Southern Myth: its origins in early literature, its flowering and ruin, as seen by white and black writers, including Twain, Faulkner, Welty, Styron, Grau, O'Connor, Wright, and Ellison.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENGL 346C
courses.title: American Fiction
paras: Special emphasis will be given to the . works of two or three major American novelists such as Herman Melville and William Faulkner. ‘ Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENGL 347A
paras: c porary American Lit e A study of American Literature from World War 2 to the present.
Prereq: ENGL 343 or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 350A/B
Seventeenth-Century Non-Dramatic Literature .

Special attention will be given to the poetry of Donne, Jonson, Herrick, Herbert, Vaughan, and Marvell and to the prose works of Bacon, Burton, and Browne. Approximately half the course will be devoted to an intensive study of Milton’s English poetry and a selection of his prose works.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 350A
courses.title: Seventeenth-Century Non-Dramatic Literature 1
paras: A study of secular and religious lyric poetry by poets such as Donne, Jonson, Herrick, Herbert, Vaughan ard Marvell. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 350B
courses.title: Seventeenth-Century Non-Dramatic Literature 2
paras: A study of selected prose works of Bacon, Burton and Browne. A more intensive study of Milton’s English poetry and a selection of his prose works.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: ENGL 362
courses.title: Shakespeare 1
paras: A study of the plays written before 1599-1600, excluding Julius Caesar. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 363
courses.title: Shakespeare 2
paras: A study of the plays written after 1599- 1600, including Jutius Caesar.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 365
courses.title: Selected Studies
paras: Designed to provide a study in depth of problems and/or authors selected by the instructor. Students interested in initiating such courses are encouraged to do so by bringing their ideas to the attention of individual instructors. Prereq: consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 373A/B
An Introduction to the History of English

The process of linguistic change as exemplified in the development of the English language from its origins in Indo-European and Germanic through modern dialects. Traditional, structural and generative approaches will be employed.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 373A
courses.title: An introduction to Historical Linguistics
paras: These lectures present language as an historical phenomenon subject to constant change. Methods of reconstruction as well as the various ways languages have undergone alteration will be discussed. Indo-European languages will be the source of examples. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 373B
courses.title: The History of English
paras: These lectures continue the discussion begun in ENGL 373A, focusing attention upon the changing English language. Phonetic, morphological, and syntactic changes as they contribute to the creation of modern English will be considered.
Prereq: ENGL 373A or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.
ENGL 3754/8

Linguistics and English Grammar Linguistics and its application to the study of grammar and language. tncluded are 1) an introduction to descriptive and historical linguistics and the principles of linguistic analysis and 2) an evaluation of English grammars ranging from the traditional to the structural and transformational-generative.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 375A
courses.title: Introduction to Descriptive Linguistics
paras: Introduction to descriptive linguistics and the principles of linguistic analysis through an examination of the phonology, forms, syntax, and semantics of English.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 375B
courses.title: Introduction to Modern English Grammar
paras: Introduction to Modern English Grammar and structure - its meaningful forms and syntax. Several methods of analysis will be employed and evaluated, including the traditional, structural, transformational-generative, and functional.
Prereq: ENGL 375A or consent o instructor. .
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 387R
courses.title: Twentieth-Century Literature 2
paras: The course complements ENGL 386R by studying the same topics in relation to modern dramas generally classified under the title of “The Theatre of the Absurd.”

ENGL 410A/B Restoration and Eighteenth-Century Literature Literature of the period that began as neo-classical, England's Augustan Age paralleling that of ancient Rome, and gradually, through subtle changes, became the precursor to the Romantic movement, giving rise, along the way, to new genres, such as comedy of manners, heroic tragedy, descriptivemeditative poetry, and the novel. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 410A
courses.title: Satire and Sense: The Restoration and Early Eighteenth Century
paras: The Restoration comedy of manners, heroic and high tragedy, poetry of the court wits and other amused commentators on society, and the major writings of Dryden, Swift, Addison, Defoe, and the early Pope. Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: ENGL 410B
courses.title: Sense and Sensibility: The Middle and Later Eighteenth Century
paras: The probing of mores and manners by Pope and Johnson, the emergence of the novel with Fielding and Sterne, and the transformation (in “the age of sensibility”) of literary attitudes and practice from classicism to romanticism.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

The Romantic Movement

Faculty of Environmental Studies

There are a number of courses offered in the Faculty of Environmental Studies of an integrative nature which extend across the academic interests of the four units, School of Architecture, Department of Geography, Department of Man-Environment Studies, and School of Urban and Regional Planning. The courses are of general interest and are open to all students in the University. There is no Department of Environmental Studies. Students interested in this area are urged to consult the course offerings of the four individual units mentioned above. These four departments/schools offer a variety of related courses allowing in-depth Studies of topics covered in the Environmental Studies courses.

courses.title: Professional Development in Environmental Management
paras: Design

The courses In design studio combine design fundamentals and design concepts, along with the opportunity to involve analysis and synthesis, professional and scientific insights, application of tools and methods for designing artifacts for man, and an awareness of the inherent physical characteristics and limitations of media and materials. The objectives of the studio are: (1) to
Course Descriptions 281

guide the student in observing aspects of the physical and social environment; to find, categorize and associate the information into fundamental structures and patterns of relationships; (2) to apply theories generated in the lecture courses to situations in the physical environment, implementing by categorizing the courses into behaviour materials, structures and mechanical systems, behaviour of man, and communications; (3) to provide the student with an opportunity to develop skill in using different “techniques” for analyzing and synthesizing problems in the physical environment; (4) to establish a relationship between faculty and students; (5) to provide a vehicle for persons from faculties of different disciplines and from outside of the university to discuss with students their problems and projects from different points of view..

courses.label: ENVS 111
courses.title: Introduction to the Study of the Future
paras: Non-technical survey of current approaches to thinking about and refining your views of the “Future”. The role of images and scenarios, : contributions of the arts and concepts of space and time. Impacts of regional science, ekistics, bioethics, synergetics, and prognostics. Paths to “inventing” the future and the comprehensive design of “optimum” environments.

courses.label: ENVS 195A
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
paras: Theories, methods and conceptual approaches that have become associated wth the study of environment are introduced. This course attempts to develop an understanding of the relationship between people and their environment.
Prereq: Environmental Studies students only. .

courses.label: ENVS 195B
courses.title: ’ introduction to Environmental Problems
paras: A discussion of some major environmental problems and issues such as the impact of urbanization of man's environment, environmental poltution, resource management, conservation, and environmental planning.

courses.label: ENVS 200
courses.title: Field Ecology
paras: Introduces the main concepts and principles of ecology: the cycling of elements; energetics and structural organization of major ecological systems; population dynamics; impact of natural resource management practices and urban and industrial development on the environment; incorporating environmental quality considerations into development activities. There are weekly field trips to study natural and disturbed ecosystems, urban and applied ecology.
Prereq: 2nd, 3rd and 4th year students only. .

courses.label: ENVS 201
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Planning Law
paras: Introduction ta legal concepts generally and to environmental and planning law concepts in particular. Designed both for students who do not plan to take further in-depth legal courses and as a prerequisite for senior legal courses ~- ENV S 401 and ENV S402. Topics to be covered include Sources of Law, Nature of Legal Remedies, Common Law, Judicial Review, Administrative Agencies and the law relating to them, Planning Act, Environmental Protection and Assessment Acts, and Federal Fisheries Act.

courses.label: ENVS 202
courses.title: Social Sclence Approaches to Environmental Problems
paras: Research strategies for the understanding and resolving of environmental problems, based upon concepts and methods derived from the social and behavioural sciences. Particular attention is given to determining the appropriate mix of research strategies for a range of problem situations in terms of data validity and reliability, time and financial constraints, and ethical considerations.
Prereq: 2nd year or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 252
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies
paras: Instruction in basic black and white photography relating to photography's role as a media tool; basic darkroom functions, camera operation, composition, photographic theory, and photo essay production. Much of the course work and projects will be done outside the classroom in field situations of environmental concern using initiative in project development. Students are expected to supply their own cameras. A limited number of cameras will be available on a rental basis. Prereq: ENV S students: others with consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 253
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies - Advanced Level
paras: Builds on work performed in the basic course. Photographic colour theory and practice, basic audio recording, editing and production, and presentation formats are investigated in workshop situations. A major project is developed using pre-research material assigned by the instructor. Students work in small groups to produce a slide-sound program of environmental concern. Prereq: ENV S 252

courses.label: ENVS 271
courses.title: Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods
paras: An introduction to scientific method: descriptive and inferential statistics: sampling design. The course emphasizes the methodological and interpretative problems involved in using selected quantitative methods to investigate selected environmental topics. .
Prereq: only for students in Environmental Studies.

courses.label: ENVS 272
courses.title: Computer Programming in Environmental Studies
paras: The course emphasizes programming skills and applications in the context of environmental problems.
Prereq: ENV S 271.

courses.label: ENVS 310
courses.title: Behavioural Studies
paras: Studies of environmental perception and of the behaviour of individuals and groups in interaction with their environment. Emphasis will be divided between an explanation of the methods of social science suitable for the study of environmental behaviour and the substantive findings from such applications.
Prereq: Second, third or fourth year students only.

courses.label: ENVS 333
courses.title: Parkland Management
paras: Systems planning, master planning and site planning for non-urban parks. Design and management for linear open space, such as rivers, trails, and coasts. Environmental nent as it relat
to amenity resources. Evaluating the effectiveness of the public participation process.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 380
courses.title: Environmental Studies Workshop
paras: An interdisciplinary workshop focusing upon environmental issues in a project or research format.

Prereq: 3rd and 4th year students in Environmental Studies; enrolment is by research team only with representatives from at least 3 units of the faculty (max. 7 people) and subject to selection of an advisor and a satisfactory project or research proposal.
Course Descriptions Environmental Studies

courses.label: ENVS 401
courses.title: Environmental Law
paras: An advanced, in-depth version of ENV S 201, providing an opportunity for detailed analysis of institutional factors regulating the natural environment and resources development in Ontario and Canada. How satistactory present statutes, court systems and boards are for improving environmental quality as well as alternatives to these legalinstitutional approaches will be discussed.
Prereq: ENV S 201

courses.label: ENVS 402
courses.title: Planning Law
paras: An analysis of the lega! basis for planning in Ontario and the practice’ of planning law as it affects planners, municipalities, local councils, property owners and residents. The roles of planning board, municipal councils, the Ontario Municipal Board, the Ministry of Housing, provincial Cabinet and the Niagara Escarpment Commission in the planning process will be discussed. Prereq: ENV S 201.

courses.label: ENVS 411
courses.title: Alternative Future Environments 1
paras: Analysis of “ideal” environments of the past, including “utopian” communities. Scrutiny of current “concepts” of future environments, including distillation of works of Bell, Clarke, Commoner, de Chardin, de Jouvenal, Dror, Doxiadis, Ehrlich, Forrester, Fuller, Kahn, Mead, Meadows, McHale, Michael, Polak, Theobald, Thompson, Toynbee, and Ward.
Prereq: 3rd or 4th year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 412
courses.title: Alternative Future Environments 2
paras: Examination of “issues” in futuristics and their “methodological” problems, with particular attention to resources utilization. Socio-Cultural Change Theory and Policy Science. Science Fiction, Extrapolation, and Technology Forecasting, Societal Indicators, Quality of Life, and Technology Assessment. Probable and Possible Urban Futures. Prereq: ENV § 411 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: ENVS 417
courses.title: Land Use History and Landscape Change 1
paras: Literature, theory and method relating to man's effects on landscapes and ecosystems. A human ecological approach. Case studies and field work.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: ENVS 444
paras: Land Evaluation and Resources. Management

The course will focus on the management of land and resources. It will emphasize the techniques of inventory, critical evatuation, and policy formulation related to sensible use of these commodities. Attitudinal, legal, and political influences will be investigated, particularty as they affect the design and implementation of planning decisions.

courses.label: ENVS 500
courses.title: Professional Development in Environmental Management
paras: Those interested in qualifying for professional status and those from other related disciplines such as civil engineering, planning, architecture, and geography may find a discussion of professional environmental management strategies useful. Issues of technical principles, data assessment, ethics, interdisciplinary work and costs will be discussed.
Prereq: 4th year students or consent of instructor.
Not Offered 1983-84.

Lab fee.

Students who have completed Ontario Grade 13 French or equivalent may take FR 192 and/or FR 195/196. Students who have little or no high school French will be placed in the appropriate beginning course, either FR 151/152 or FR 155 for ane or two terms. courses.label: GEOG 101
courses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
paras: An introduction to human geography through a survey of some of the concepts, methods, techniques and applications of geographic analysis to man's cultural environment. Directed towards the man-land theme and the location analysis theme.

courses.label: GEOG 102
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
paras: Emphasis on the natural environment as an integrated system of which it is a part. Selected aspects of weather - climate, water, soils, biota, landforms along with flows of energy, water and matter and their resultant effects on the subsystems of the natural environment are studied.

courses.label: GEOG 110
courses.title: Introduction to the Field of Geography
paras: The goats of this course are to introduce first year geographers to: Geography as a profession, different approaches to solving geographical problems, research report writing, and to the Geography program at the University of Waterloo.
Prereq: First year Geography Majors only or 1st year Arts students intending to major in Geography or consent of instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 125R
courses.title: Introduction to the Third World
paras: A thematic approach to such topics as population issues, planning and practices; education and heaith in the social development process; urbanization and industrialization; Planning for rural and urban development in Asia, Africa and Latin America.

courses.label: GEOG 127
courses.title: Regional Problems of Europe
paras: An introduction to the Geography of Europe which examines agricultural, industrial and urban problems. Lectures, discussions and visual presentations based on field experience of instructors.

courses.label: GEOG 201
courses.title: Some Basic Topics of Physical
paras: 2ography : irther studies of energy and matter ws in the atmosphere and on the land. Specific topics include radiation, energy and circulation regimes of the rth-atmosphere system and the dyna- ‘cs and morphology of earth struccures, stream systems and glacial landform systems. mvareq: GEOG 102.

courses.label: GEOG 203
courses.title: >ome Basic Topics of Cultural and Regional Geography
paras: *he approach of the regional eographer is illustrated by reference to ne or more world regions. Political, social and historical processes are studied as they affect man's perceptions f his environment and the jentification of culture regions. .rereq: A Ist year human geography course.

courses.label: GEOG 204
courses.title: Iovlet Union
paras: Introduction to the geography of the Soviet Union, with a focus on selected yroblems in urbanization, ndustrialization, resource use and egional economic development in a planned economy.

courses.label: GEOG 206B
paras: ‘frica rhe geography of modern Africa south of the Sahara in the context of changing attitudes to the continent on the part of he “developed” countries. Attention will acus on problems of the physical, social and economic environments.

courses.label: GEOG 220
courses.title: World Regional Geography
paras: Study in depth of selected areas of the world's climatic regions, emphasizing characteristic problems as well as their physical, cultural and economic interrelationships. Utilization of natural resources, the effects of increasing population density, the occupance and utilization of urban and rural lands, and the effects of man’s tools, techniques and institutions on the earth's surface.

courses.label: GEOG 221
courses.title: The United States
paras: Focuses on population shifts, environmental issues, and regional economic development in the context of the nation and selected regions.

courses.label: GEOG 225R
courses.title: Urbanization In the Third World
paras: An analysis of the factors behind the rapid urbanization of selected areas in Asia, Africa and Latin America, with an examination of related problems of urban planning and development control policies.
Prereq: Any Faculty of Environmental Studies course.

courses.label: GEOG 232
courses.title: Geography of Population
paras: Population of geography and its relationship to demography and human ecology. Analysis of the growth, diffusion, and distribution of human populations throughout the world.

courses.label: GEOG 251
courses.title: Cities in Canada
paras: An introduction to some basic concepts in urban studies emphasizing a systematic approach to processes and problems of urban development in Canada.

courses.label: GEOG 260
courses.title: Introduction to Cartography and Map
paras: Analysis

Basic concepts involved in the analysis and use of existing types of cartographic products. Background theory of the production and reproduction of topographic and thematic maps, including historical development, collection of data and symbolization.

courses.label: GEOG 275
courses.title: Introductory Alr Photo Analysis and Remote Sensing
paras: Basic techniques of handling air photos, viewing them stereoscopically (in 3D), identifying and describing features, making measurements and general use in the broad field of geographic and environmental studies. Introduction to specialized types of air photos, sateltite imagery and remote sensing techniques.
Lab fee $15-$20.

courses.label: GEOG 300
courses.title: Geomorphology and the Southern Ontarlo Environment
paras: Emphasizes field work and field trips in exploring the evolution of S. Ontario landforms. The identification of landforms, landform assemblages and their relationships. The meaning and utility of this information in terms of the contemporary and future environment will be stressed.
Prereq: GEOG 201, or consent of instructor. Third and Fourth Year Students only.
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 301
courses.title: Climatology
paras: Advanced study of the elements and mechanics of climate and weather. Analysis of world climatic and weather patterns. Effects of climate on man's activities and on the distribution of natural vegetation and soils. Weather forecasting. Applied climatology. Prereq: GEOG 201.

courses.label: GEOG 302
courses.title: Geomorphical Process
paras: The impact of processes in jandform development and modification. Techniques of measurement particularly as they show the impact of changes under different climatic conditions and processes connected with glaciation and deglaciation, and eolian. karst, coastal and fluvial landforms.
Prereq: Third and fourth year students only with GEOG 201 or consent of instructor.
Lab fee $10.

courses.label: GEOG 303
courses.title: Physical Basis and the Geography of Water
paras: Specific topics inctude: the earth’s water balance and cycle, oceans, lakes and swamps, snow cover, ground ice, glacier ice and streams. Attention is directed to the impact of water on the earth's surface, the role of water in the earth’s system, and water as a resource and hazard. Some field work.
Prereq: GEOG 201, or consent of instructor..

courses.label: GEOG 307
courses.title: Social Survey Techniques
paras: Social research and the planning process; interview and self administered surveys; questionnaire design; profile data; sampling; data processing; nonsurvey data collection techniques; practical applications.
Prereq: Second or third year Geography Students and ENV S 271; other ENV S students with‘consent of instructor. Cross-listed as PLAN 307.

courses.label: GEOG 311
courses.title: Regional Industrial Development
paras: Manufacturing and transportation in the context of economic development at regional and urban scales. Aims at deepening conceptual insights and fostering appreciation of their relevance to understanding particular areas. Empirical focus on Canada and the U.K. Prereq: GEOG 202 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 315
courses.title: Agricultural Geography
paras: The geographical dimensions of agricultural systems. issues include the diffusion of innovations, regional evolution of agricultural structure and vertical integration. Comparative study of programs of government intervention in agriculture in Canada and Europe. Some field trips.
Prereq: GEOG 202 or consent of instructor.

Prereq: ENV S 271 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Economic and Social Techniques for Regional Planning
paras: Study and critical appraisal of a selection of descriptive and evaluative regional analysis techniques in common use. Reliability and applicability will be reviewed. Emphasis given to economic considerations of regional development. Discussion of input-output analysis; cost-benefit analysis, planning, programming and budgeting systems; and social area analysis. Same as Plan 319..
Prereq: ECON 101, 102 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Geographical Study of Canada Geographical basis of Canada and
paras: Canadian issues. Selected problems relating to nationalism, regionalism, environmental quality, urbanization, regional disparities and resource development.

paras: A geographical analysis of selected regions and current problems. The theme chosen in any given year will vary.

courses.title: Special Topics in Development of the
paras: Third World , . Emphasis on research methods and approaches to the study of geographic aspects of selected social and economic development problems. Regions of concentration will be mainly tropical Africa, South and South-East Asia, Caribbean and tropical Latin America. Among topics selected are population, agriculture and food, rural development urbanization, resource development an. regional planning.
Prereq: First or second year courses related to Third World studies or consent of instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 331
courses.title: Special Topics in Cultural Geography
paras: A detailed investigation of selected issues in man's relations with the natural environment. Given as a seminar, issues will be partially selected on the basis of the interests of participants. Prereq: GEOG 330 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 332
courses.title: Special Topics in the Geography of Population
paras: Detailed study of selected topics of population geography.
Prereq: 2nd year students or higher.

courses.label: GEOG 341
courses.title: Historical Geography of Canada 1
paras: The changing geographies of settlement and resource use from the Discoveries to the early nineteenth century.
Prereq: A second year human geography course or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 342
courses.title: Historical Geography of Canada 2
paras: The changing geographies of settlement and resource use in the nineteenth and. early twentieth centuries.
Prereq: A second year human geography course or consent of instructor.

frontier problems, the location of capital “ities, internal organization of states, xernal relations, and geopolitics. ereq: A 2nd year human geography course or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Air Photo Interpretation
paras: The principles of air photo interpretation utilizing specific criteria visible in the conventional air photo. Examples from local and foreign environments.

courses.title: Environmental Remote Sensing
paras: Theoretical and practical aspects of remote sensing (RS). Interaction - between electromagnetic radiation, environmental media and sensors. Analysis of non-photographic systems like RADAR and LANDSAT. Methods of RS data processing and analysis and the application of RS techniques to studies of physical and human environments.
Prereq: GEOG 275
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 381
courses.title: The Nature of Geography
paras: The roots and evatution of geographic thought: conceptual approaches and pathways. Past traditions, current issues, and future trends. The politics and sociology of geography as an art, science, and profession.
Prereq: Any three GEOG credits or consent of instructor.
Lab fee $10.

courses.title: Senior Honours Research Essay Proposal
paras: Participants are responsible for developing a research proposal under the supervision of an appropriate faculty member. Normally taken in the third year. , Prereq: Honours Geography students only; cannot be counted for credit towards a general degree.

courses.label: GEOG 391
courses.title: Fleld Research
paras: One week field camp session during which a specific area will be analysed from a geographic point of view. Students will be expected to undertake individual or group analysis of specific probiems and must present the resuits in a written report.
Prereq: Third Year Honours Geography students only; cannot be counted for credit towards a general degree. Estimated cost to student: $100-$120.

courses.label: GEOG 400
courses.title: Climatic and Periglacial Morphology
paras: Characteristics of the main principles of climatic and climatogenetic geomorphology. Examination of processes and forms related to the periglacial environment.
Prereq: One of GEOG 300, GEOG 302 or EARTH 342 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: GEOG 401
courses.title: Glacial Geomorphology and Some Contemporary Applications
paras: Advanced study of the total effect of glaciation. Glacial and fluvioglacial erosion and deposition and their effects on landscapes will be analyzed. Special attention on the environmental influences of glaciation and on practical applications of glacial geomorphologists’ techniques and information. Prereq: One of GEOG 300, GEOG 302 or EARTH 342.

courses.label: GEOG 403
courses.title: Advanced Cartography 1
paras: Advanced study of numerical map analysis and computer mapping techniques.
Prereq: GEOG 260, and ENV § 271.

courses.title: Advanced Cartography 2
paras: Advanced study of the basic techniques of map production, the theory of cartographic communication and map design. Technical aspects include photo mechanics, scribing, process photography, typography, proofing and printing processes. Theoretical topics include the map as a communications system, advanced map design and principles of information selection and generalization.
Prereq: GEOG 360
Lab fee $25.

courses.label: GEOG 406
courses.title: Tropical Geomorphology
paras: Basic geomorphological concepts and their application in a tropical environment. Special emphasis on morphology and processes as related to the geological foundation.
Prereq: One of GEOG 300, GEOG 302, EARTH 342 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Fleid and Lab Techniques In Geomorphology
paras: An analysis of the range of techniques used by geomorphologists. This course will involve intensive field surveying, mapping and laboratory work.

paras: A companion course to GEOG 311. Emphasis on decision-making, multinational corporations, technologi¢al change, and analyses of the locational patterns of specific industries.
Prereq: GEOG 311

courses.title: Energy Resources Management
paras: Energy management theories and methods emphasizing ecological and economic approaches. Issues related to managing conventional energy resources and development of alternatives. Techniques for studying energy issues are also presented. Prereq: GEOG 359 and either GEOG 311 or GEOG 356 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Europe and the Mediterranean
paras: Detailed study of physical, cultural, economic and political geography, including the development of cities, problems of agriculture, changing industrial patterns, distribution of trade, regional disparities, and planning on the city, regional and national Jevels.

courses.title: Canada
paras: Seminar on the geographical analysis of selected Canadian topics. Emphasis on regional synthesis and topics of continuing Canadian concern.

Course Descriptions

courses.label: HLTH 140
courses.title: Introduction to Health Sciences 1
paras: An exploration of the biological basis of health and disease, strategies for prevention and treatment of disease, and the moral, social, and psychological

impact of innovations in health care on Canadian society. Topics include human reproduction, (conception, pregnancy and chiidbirth, sexual development and expression), human heredity (chromosomal disorders, genetic diseases, birth defects}, and acute disease states (infectious diseases, cancer, immune deficiencies).

courses.label: HLTH 141
courses.title: Introduction to Health Sciences 2
paras: An exploration of the biological basis of health and disease, strategies for prevention and treatment of disease, and the moral, social, and psychological impact of innovations in health care on Canadian society. Topics include the human nervous system (neurological disorders, mental illness, brain dysfunctions, drug abuse), lifestyles and health (heart disease, obesity, exercise, smoking), and health care systems (environmental health, medical abuses, aging, and dying).

courses.label: HLTH 220
courses.title: Health and the Family
paras: The course familiarizes students with the issues involved in understanding how people live and develop within the context of families, and the family interaction with the larger social community. Special emphasis will be placed on health related concerns and the ways in which the family and health care institutions of the society contribute to the physical and emotional health of its members. Prereq: HLTH 140 and 141

courses.label: HLTH 241
courses.title: Disease Process
paras: An introduction to the study of factors governing the'occurrence of diseases in human populations, using selected diseases to illustrate disease mechanisms and identification of risk factors. Prereq: BIOL 230, 233, KIN 317 or equivalent.

courses.label: HLTH 245
courses.title: Community Health
paras: This course examines health care delivery systems by considering organizational principles, manpower issues, health resources and economics, service utilization and alternatives to the institutional model. There is a focus on societal and political issues which affect the health of the society through the delivery system.
Prereq: Health Studies students only, or permission of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 302
courses.title: Introduction to Biomathematics 1 (MTHEL. 302a) Biometry is a biological
paras: discipline requiring both a knowledge of mathematics and some basic understanding of specific biological phenomena. The course material has been selected from genetics and gerontology to provide examples of where both mathematics and biology have contributed to the advancement of knowledge in interdisciplinary areas. Prereq: KIN 116 or first year Chemistry or consent of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 303
courses.title: Introduction to Biomathematics 2
paras: (MTHEL 302b) A continuation of Biomathematics 1. Topics considered are first order reaction kinetics in biological systems including a discussion of radioisotope and C'4 dating, higher order kinetics including Statistical considerations in enzyme kinetics, models for and the measurement of evolution from a knowledge of genetics and protein structure and assessing the relative importance of evironmental factors as evolutionary determinants.
Prereq: HLTH 302.

courses.label: HLTH 340
courses.title: Environmental Health
paras: An examination of the effects of environmental pollutants and occupational hazards on human health. Emphasis will be placed on the biological mechanisms by which environmental toxicants.cause human disease and disability.
Prereq: KIN 317 or equivalent.

courses.label: HLTH 344
courses.title: Program Evaluation
paras: A comprehensive and systematic introduction to the key concepts, methodologies, and issues related to program evaluation in general and their application to health programs in particular. Administrative and poticy implications as well as the technical/ methodological evaluation issues that face individuals involved in administering, planning, implementing, and evaluating health programs will be discussed.
Prereq: Basic courses in Statistics and in Research Design.

courses.label: HLTH 346
courses.title: Nutrition (KIN 346)
paras: An elementary course in nutrition with
special emphasis on diet for sport and certain physiological conditions. Prereq: KIN 317 or equivalent.

courses.label: HLTH 348
courses.title: Social Psychology of Health Behaviour
paras: (KIN 348) The study and application of basic social psychological processes in relation to selected health-related behaviours (e.g. family planning, overeating, smoking, non-medical drug use, cardiovascular risk factors, patient compliance, medical care utilization). Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 349
courses.title: Principles of Behaviour Modification
paras: (KIN 349) A course providing a general overview of behaviour modification principles and procedures. Basic principles of reinforcement, punishment, modelling and desensitization are examined as they relate to health behaviour.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 407
courses.title: Physiology of Coronary Heart Disease
paras: {KIN 407) An examination of the pathology, risk factors and rehabilitation programs related to coronary heart disease. Major emphasis is placed on the cardio-respiratory implications of exercise in the rehabilitation process.
Prereq: KIN 300 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 410
courses.title: Growth, Development and Aging
paras: (KIN 410) The physiology of human growth, development and aging is examined, with special reference to the influence of diet, environment, exercise and disease on the normal processes. Prereq: KIN 200, BIOL 230 and 233.

courses.label: HLTH 431
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes an approved proposal and completion of the first three chapters of the thesis — Introduction, Review of Literature, and Methods.

courses.label: HLTH 432
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes data collection, data analysis and presentation of results in thesis form.
Prereq: Completion of HLTH 431.

courses.label: HLTH 442
courses.title: Epldemiology of Chronic Diseases
paras: An investigation of the epidemiology of selected non-communicable diseases. The course emphasizes understanding of epidemiologic methods and identification of risk factors. Specific diseases examined will vary from year to year.
Prereq: HLTH 241 and an introductory Statistics course or consent of instructor.

courses.label: HLTH 443
courses.title: Behaviour and Chronic Disease
paras: A critical analysis of various behavioural strategies for the prevention of coronary heart disease, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and lung cancer. The role of behaviour in the pathogenesis of disease and the feasibility of behavioural change for prevention of disease will be discussed. Prereq: HLTH 344, 348, 349.

courses.label: HLTH 445
courses.title: Semi in Health Pr th
paras: A study of current issues pertaining to health.promotion, health behaviour, or biomedical research. Topics may include pertinent research that is significant to the health of individuals, families and groups, or the community. Prereq: Health Studies students only. Normally only 4th year students will be admitted.

courses.label: HLTH 472
courses.title: Independent Study
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a student's project prior to registration. May be repeated in subsequent terms. Prereq: Consult with Department.

courses.label: HIST 100
courses.title: Landmarks In World History
paras: A thematic introduction to the development of the world's major civilizations. This year’s theme is “Community and Social Order”, examining the dynamic relationship between individuals and their social structures, and their state.

courses.label: HIST 102A
courses.title: The American Identity 1607-1980
paras: A consideration of the shaping of American characteristics under the headings of: The Frontier; Religious Denominationalism; Libertarian Revolution; Black Slavery; New Immigrations; Mass Production; the Great Depression; War and Global Americanism.

courses.label: HIST 102B
courses.title: Imperialism in the Twentieth Century
paras: An introduction to the colonial experience and to the processes of national emergence in the twentieth century. Special reference is made to the Caribbean area.

courses.label: HIST 102C
courses.title: The Origins of Wars in the Twentieth Century
paras: An analysis of the diplomatic, political, economic, ideological, social and cultural explanations of the causes of the major wars of this century with special emphasis on Canada.

courses.label: HIST 102D
courses.title: From Nationalism to Totalitarianism
paras: The growth of nationalism and nation states since the French Revolution with attention to the Industrial Revolution, the World Wars, Fascism, Naziism and Stalinism.
Offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: HIST 102E
courses.title: Canadian History
paras: Selected major themes from pioneer life to Canadian involvement in twentieth century wars.
Offered at St. Jerome's Callege.

courses.label: HIST 102F
courses.title: An Introduction to Western Intellectual History Since the Renaissance
paras: An exploration of some of the questions and answers posed by thinkers on the human predicament from Renaissance and Reformation times to the modern period. Readings range from Luther to J.P. Sartre, Shakespeare to Marx and Freud.

courses.label: HIST 102H
courses.title: Early Modern Europe
paras: This course will survey the chief features of early modern European society. Topics will include the Renaissance and Reformation, Old Regime society, the scientific revolution, the Enlightenment and the French Revolution.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 102M
courses.title: Law and Society in the Middle Ages
paras: A study of the sociat and political fabric.

the laws and legal! procedures of the Midclle Ages. Barbarian Codes, Feudal Law and rediscovered Roman Law will be examined along with legal procedures and institutions such as oaths, ordeals and the Inquisition. Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 130
courses.title: The Modern World in Historical Perspective
paras: This course will introduce students, through the interrelationships and interaction of selected themes, to the contemporary history of Europe. North America, and the Far East. Its format includes two interpretive tectures per week plus major films on twentieth century crises and optional discussion groups.

courses.label: HIST 200
courses.title: Twentieth Century History as Documented by Films
paras: Ahistory of the twentieth century through films. The First World War, , Europe between the Wars, the Second World War, North American society in the twentieth century and other political, moral and social themes will be explored.

courses.label: HIST 201X
courses.title: Canadian Urban History
paras: An historical examination of the
- urbanization process, the social, political and economic factors that shaped the Canadian city, and the relationship between selected metropolitan and hinterland areas.

courses.label: HIST 202X
courses.title: The Individual and the Family in History
paras: A survey of the changes in the quality and structure of life with special emphasis on love, marriage and the family in the West since the sixteenth century.
Offered at St_ Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 203X
courses.title: Modern Quebec
paras: The course will discuss the problem of Quebec in contemporary Canada by analyzing the historical background of key issues like separatism, the survival of the French language, French- Canadian nationalism and the Quiet Revolution.

courses.label: HIST 205X
courses.title: Canadian Business History
paras: A study of the development of business in Canada at both the general economic and the individual enterprise level.

courses.label: HIST 206X
courses.title: History of Canadian Minorities
paras: An introduction to the history of selected racial and regional minorities in Canada. The course examines the emergence of minority communities, and their position in modern Canadian society.

courses.label: HIST 208
courses.title: The Cold War: American-Russian
paras: Relati Since Ni ber, 1917

An examination of this confrontation by traditionalist and revisionist (New Left) historians: Wilson versus Lenin, 1917; Roosevelt, Truman and Stalin; post 1945 — containment, co-existence, and critics.

courses.label: HIST 209X
courses.title: Twentieth Century America 1898-1978
paras: An examination of the title theme with particular emphasis on the United States’ emergence as a worid power: the Cold War, J.F.K. and the New Frontier, the October 1962 missile crisis, Vietnam, L.B.J. and the Great Society, the 1970's in retrospect.

courses.label: HIST 210X
courses.title: History of Law
paras: An historical introduction to law throughout the ages: concepts.
institutions, practices.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 211
courses.title: British History to 1603
paras: A survey of the main stages in the transition of Britain fram a remote province of the Roman Empire to a prominent state of post-Reformation Europe. Within the chronological framework, political and constitutional as well as ecclesiastical and social developments will be examined.

courses.label: HIST 212
courses.title: British History since 1603
paras: A survey of the shaping of British society and the British experience from the time of Shakespeare to the present: constitutional conflict and compromise, rise and fall of empire, industrial and urban revolution, world wars and welfare state.

courses.label: HIST 213X
courses.title: Modern Western Popular Culture
paras: This course examines historically the formation of a distinct modern western popular culture, looking primarily at Britain, France, Canada and the United States from around 1850 to the present, and emphasizing such aspects as: industrialism and leisure, the family anc. sexual attitudes, religion and popular belief. education and literacy. drinking habits, organized sport and mass entertainment.

courses.label: HIST 216
courses.title: Irish History: Achievement, Unification, Revolt
paras: Political, social and religious history of treland from the beginning of the golden age of Irish medieval civilization to the Act of Union, c. 400 to 1800.

courses.label: HIST 217
courses.title: Irish History: The Nineteenth and Twentieth Centuries
paras: Political, social and religious history of Ireland emphasizing social changes, the struggle for Home Rule and the Republic, 1800 to present.

courses.label: HIST 222
courses.title: History of Modern Revolutions
paras: An introduction to historical explanations of revolutions with special focus on social change and revolutionary theories. The French, Russian and Chinese Revolutions will be used as case studies.
Offered at Renison College.

courses.label: HIST 223
courses.title: Canadian Culture and Society to 1900
paras: An inquiry into the nature of the Canadian experience by examining concepts and themes that were significant before the twentieth century.

courses.label: HIST 224
courses.title: Canadian Culture and Society in the Twentieth Century
paras: An approach to modern Canadian development as the people have wrestled with such phenomena as: war, depression, internal and external tensions, urban growth, the "post industrial" society.

courses.label: HIST 226
courses.title: The Middle East Conflict
paras: A survey of regional. religious and imperial rivalries from ancient to modern times, with emphasis on the twentieth century and the Arab-Israeli conflict.
Offered at Conrad Grebe! College.

courses.title: History of Medieval Europe 814-1303
paras: The political, cultural, economic and ecclesiastical development of Europe from Chariemagne to Philip IV of France.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 252X
courses.title: Europe in the Nineteenth Century
paras: European social and culturat history, 1815-1914. This course will consider the inter-relations between ideas and institutions during a period of industrialization, ubanization and mass education.

courses.label: HIST 253X
courses.title: Canadian History: The British Period
paras: The evolution of Canadian society in the face of dominant British and American influences.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: HIST 254X
courses.title: Canadian History: The National Period
paras: This course studies the development of Modern Canada. Themes of the course include immigration, industrialization, feminism, labour unrest, and regionalism.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College in Winter term.

courses.label: HIST 255X
courses.title: British Empire and Commonwealth
paras: A wide-ranging survey. The first lecture each week will provide a narrative framework, the second, illustrative detail. At weekly seminars students will discuss, successively, significant individuals, colonies, commodities, institutions, documents and books which they have chosen and researched for themselves.

courses.label: HIST 256X
courses.title: History of the United States since 1865
paras: A survey of American society, politics and thought and of the relations of the United States with the outside world from 1865 to the present.

courses.label: HIST 257
courses.title: History of the United States until 1865 The settlement of English North
paras: America, British colonial society, the American Revolution, politics and culture in the American Republic, the Civil War. A special emphasis on religious and political culture.

courses.label: HIST 300
courses.title: The Idea of History
paras: The course is an introduction to the Philosophy of History and to the art of historical writing. It deals with the great theoretical issues influencing historical analysis and with the classics of historical literature. it is equally concerned with the practical problems of historical research.

courses.label: HIST 305
courses.title: English History 1485-1603
paras: A study of achievements and crises in - politics and society, and of changes and continuities in religion and philosophy in the Tudor period.

courses.label: HIST 307
courses.title: British History 1760-1867
paras: A study of people, power, thought and culture in the world's first industrializing
society.

courses.label: HIST 308
courses.title: Britain Since 1867
paras: A study of the British experience and of Britain's part in world history from the 1860's to the 1980's.

courses.label: HIST 311
courses.title: Western European Cultural History
paras: A canvass of European thought between 1600 and 1950, on questions of self, society, science and spirituality.

courses.label: HIST 319
courses.title: French-Canadian History
paras: An examination of Pre-industrial French Canada with emphasis on the cultural, political and economic themes which form the background to Modern Quebec history.

courses.label: HIST 320
courses.title: The History of Modern Quebec
paras: The course will treat the history of Quebec from 1867 to the present. Nationalism, separatism, language and cultural problems, economic and social issues are all examined in their historical context.

courses.label: HIST 321
courses.title: History of Canadian-American Relations to 1914
paras: An examination of the history of relations between the two countries until 1914. Topics of a political, economic, social and cultural nature will be studied.

courses.label: HIST 322
courses.title: History of Canadian-American
paras: Relations since 1914
An examination of the history of relations between the two countries since 1914. Topics of a political, economic, social and cultural nature will be studied.

courses.label: HIST 325
courses.title: History of Canadian Indians to 1870's “From Freedom to Conquest”. The history of Indian-white contact and its
paras: effect on the life and culture of the native Canadians.

courses.label: HIST 329
courses.title: History of Anglo-American Law
paras: The emphasis will be on the early development of the common taw in England and the formulation of constitutional law in the United States. Offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: HIST 343
courses.title: Mystical and Utopian Movements from the 12th to the 17th Century 1
paras: A study of the recurring dream of the coming golden age in the High Middle Ages beginning with Joachim of Fiore, including the Spiritual Franciscans and the Taborites, and ending with the Revolutionary of the Upper Rhine. Offered at Conrad Grebe! College.

courses.label: HIST 345
courses.title: Minorities in International Perspective
paras: An examination of the minorities phenomenon in the context of national, regional, and international power struggles and the resulting discriminations, reftugee movements, international dispersions, and conflicts in new settings. Emphasis on twentieth century.
Offered at Conrad Grebe} College

courses.label: HIST 346
courses.title: Mennonite History: Canadian Issues
paras: Special issues examined in historical context include church/state conflicts in education, conscription and: social poticies, and such phenomena as nonconformity, internal divisions, organizational proliferation, thealogical shifts, changing forms of leadership, and issues of identity.
Offered at Conrad Grebe! College.

Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 350
courses.title: West Indian History
paras: A study of the Caribbean region from aboriginal times, including European imperialism, the history of plantations, slavery and slave society, independence movements, and the problems posed by modernization, underdevelopment and neo-colonialism.

courses.label: HIST 358

paras: The development of Germany from the Austrian-Prussian rivalry of 1740 through the end of World War II. Offered at Renison College.

paras: An analysis of the economic changes, the rise of “new monarchs", the nature and effect of the “religious reformation”, the expansion of Europe to the “new world” with their implications for sixteenth century Europe.
Offered at Renison College.

paras: The course will examine the growth of Ontario from a pioneer settlement, with particular emphasis on economic, social, political and culturat aspects of change. An emphasis will also be placed on the sources and methods of local historical research.

courses.label: HIST 387
courses.title: Ontario History since Confederation
paras: The course will examine the emergence of Ontario as an industrial giant and the development of its hegemony in Canada. An emphasis wiil also be placed on the sources and methods of local historical research.

courses.label: KIN 102
courses.title: Biophysical Basts of Kinesialogy
paras: Human physical movement is discussed from mechanical, anatomical and physiological viewpoints. The course provides a general orientation to the study of Kinesiology..

courses.label: KIN 103
courses.title: Psycho-Social Basis of Kinesiology
paras: An introduction to the study of human physical activity from psychological, sociological, anthropological and historical perspectives.

courses.label: KIN 116
courses.title: General and Organic Chemistry
paras: An introduction to the chemical concepts of importance in kinesiology and health studies.

courses.label: KIN 200
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Limbs and Trunk
paras: Functionally-oriented study of the limbs and trunk by regions using predissected cadavers. A brief introduction to Neuroanatomy is included.
Prereq: Kinesiology, Health Studies and Dance students or permission of instructor. No Year 1 students are admitted. ‘

courses.label: KIN 201
courses.title: Human Anatomy of the Brain, Head and Neck
paras: The anatomical structure and function of the brain, cranial nerves and sense organs of the head are emphasized. Included is an introduction to the histology of the nervous system. An opportunity for some dissection of the head and neck is provided.
Prereq: KIN 200 or consent of Instructor
